nodes.statement: Independent coordinates have product weights. Expectations of product observables factor, and transporting weights along a function commutes with expectation.
nodes.label: lem:weighted-product

nodes.statement: Distribute products over finite sums; for pushforward interchange the two sums and evaluate each fiber indicator.

nodes.name: Bridges between the expectation APIs
nodes.statement: The finite average is Mathlib's finite expectation, $\operatorname{avg}(f)=\E_{a\in A}f(a)$ (\texttt{Finset.expect}); both vanish on an empty type. On a nonempty type the independent product of uniform distributions on $A$, indexed by a finite set $I$, is the uniform distribution on $A^I$. Hence $\mathrm{expList}$ over $T$ rounds is the expectation of $F$ over $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform draws, both as Mathlib's $\E_{\omega\colon\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\to A}$ and under the product distribution.
nodes.label: lem:bridge

nodes.statement: Mathlib's finite expectation is a sum divided by a cardinality. Every point of $A^I$ has product weight $|A|^{-|I|}=|A^I|^{-1}$. Combine both with Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-trajectory}.

nodes.name: Transition kernel
nodes.statement: A finite kernel assigns a distribution to every state. Its operator iterates compute expectations at finite times; trajectory functionals additionally record the history.
nodes.label: def:kernel

nodes.name: Endpoint agreement
nodes.statement: Ignoring history in a trajectory expectation recovers the iterated transition operator.
nodes.label: lem:endpoint

nodes.name: Existence of stationary weights
nodes.statement: Every stochastic kernel on a nonempty finite type has a distribution $p$ with $pK=p$.
nodes.label: thm:stationary

nodes.statement: Average the first $n+1$ evolved distributions. The stationarity defect of this Ces\`aro average is $(p_{n+1}-p_0)/(n+1)$, which tends to zero coordinatewise. Compactness of the finite probability simplex gives a convergent subsequence; continuity of finite sums implies that its limit is stationary.

nodes.name: Uniform absorption block
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a zero-one survival indicator with $Kf\le f$. Suppose for each state $a$ there is $n_a$ with $(K^{n_a}f)(a)<1$. There are $m>0$ and $0\le q<1$ such that $K^m f\le qf$.
nodes.label: lem:block

nodes.statement: Take one plus the maximum of the finitely many access times. Antitonicity of survival probabilities puts every state below one at that time. Their finite maximum supplies $q$. At states with $f=0$, absorption keeps the expectation zero.

nodes.name: Geometric decay and convergence
nodes.statement: Under these hypotheses, $K^{nm}f\le q^n f$, and $K^t f(a)\to0$ for every state $a$.
nodes.label: thm:absorption

nodes.statement: Induct over blocks using positivity and linearity. The geometric bound tends to zero. For arbitrary $t$, compare with $m\lfloor t/m\rfloor$ by antitonicity.

nodes.name: Finite-horizon optional stopping
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi$ equal $\varphi_A$ on an event $A$ and $\varphi_B$ on an event $B$, and let $S$ be the event of lying in neither. If $\E_{x_0}\varphi(X_T)=\varphi(x_0)$ and $m\le\varphi-\varphi_B\le M$ on $S$, then $\varphi(x_0)-\varphi_B-(\varphi_A-\varphi_B)\Pr_{x_0}(X_T\in A)$ lies between $m\Pr_{x_0}(X_T\in S)$ and $M\Pr_{x_0}(X_T\in S)$. Hence, if $\varphi_A\ne\varphi_B$, the conservation law holds for every $T$ and $\Pr_{x_0}(X_T\in S)\to0$, then $\Pr_{x_0}(X_T\in A)\to(\varphi(x_0)-\varphi_B)/(\varphi_A-\varphi_B)$; if moreover $A$ is absorbing, this is the supremum of the finite-time probabilities.
nodes.label: thm:optional-stopping

nodes.statement: Pointwise, $\varphi-\varphi_B=(\varphi_A-\varphi_B)1_A+(\varphi-\varphi_B)1_S$ (on $A\cap B$ both sides vanish). Take expectations at time $T$ and bound the last term by monotonicity. For the limit, take $M=-m=\sum_a|\varphi(a)-\varphi_B|$ and squeeze. If $A$ is absorbing, the finite-time probabilities increase, so their limit is their supremum.

nodes.name: Kernel of a round-based process
nodes.statement: A deterministic update $\mathrm{step}\colon S\times R\to S$ driven by a uniform round $r\in R$ defines the kernel $K(s)=\mathrm{law}(\mathrm{step}(s,r))$. Its $T$-step expectations are expectations over $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds.
nodes.label: def:ofstep

nodes.statement: Induction on $T$, unfolding one round of $\mathrm{expList}$.

nodes.name: Time reversal of i.i.d.\ rounds
nodes.statement: For every functional $F$ of $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds, $\E F(r_T,\dots,r_1)=\E F(r_1,\dots,r_T)$. In particular the $T$-step expectations of a round-based process are also obtained by applying the rounds last to first.
nodes.label: thm:reverse

nodes.statement: Write both sides as uniform averages over $\mathrm{Fin}\,T\to R$ and reindex by the involution $i\mapsto T-1-i$.

nodes.name: Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities
nodes.statement: Let $X=\sum_{i<n}Y_i(\omega_i)$ with independent uniform coordinates. If each $Y_i$ is $\{0,1\}$-valued, $\Pr(X\ge\E X+\lambda)\le e^{-2\lambda^2/n}$. If $Y_i-\E Y_i\le b$ and $\sum_i\mathrm{Var}\,Y_i\le\sigma^2$, then $\Pr(X\ge\E X+\lambda)\le\exp\bigl(-\lambda^2/(2\sigma^2(1+b\lambda/(3\sigma^2)))\bigr)$.
nodes.label: thm:concentration

nodes.statement: Markov's inequality applied to $e^{tX}$, which factors over the coordinates. Hoeffding's lemma bounds each Bernoulli factor; for Bernstein, $e^y\le1+y+y^2/(2(1-u/3))$ for $y\le u<3$ bounds each factor, and $t$ is chosen as $\lambda/(\sigma^2+b\lambda/3)$.

nodes.name: Chernoff bounds for independent Bernoulli trials
nodes.statement: Let $X=\sum_iX_i$ be a sum of independent $\{0,1\}$-valued trials with $\Pr(X_i=1)=p_i$, and let $\mu_L\le\mu=\sum_ip_i\le\mu_H$. For $\delta>0$, \[\Pr(X\ge(1+\delta)\mu_H)\le\Bigl(\frac{e^{\delta}}{(1+\delta)^{1+\delta}}\Bigr)^{\mu_H} \le e^{-\delta^2\mu_H/(2+\delta)},\] and for $0<\delta<1$, \[\Pr(X\le(1-\delta)\mu_L)\le\Bigl(\frac{e^{-\delta}}{(1-\delta)^{1-\delta}}\Bigr)^{\mu_L} \le e^{-\delta^2\mu_L/2}.\] The trials are $\{0,1\}$-valued observables of the coordinates of an independent product of distributions, independent biased coins (counting the heads in any subset), or the coordinates of one uniform round (Mitzenmacher--Upfal, \emph{Probability and Computing}, Theorems 4.4 and 4.5 with Exercise 4.7).
nodes.label: thm:chernoff

nodes.statement: Markov's inequality applied to $e^{tX}$, which factors over the coordinates; each factor is $1+p_i(e^t-1)\le e^{p_i(e^t-1)}$, so $\E e^{tX}\le e^{\mu_H(e^t-1)}$ for $t\ge0$ and $\E e^{tX}\le e^{\mu_L(e^t-1)}$ for $t\le0$. Take $t=\log(1+\delta)$, respectively $t=\log(1-\delta)$. The closed forms follow from $\log(1+\delta)\ge2\delta/(2+\delta)$ (the first term of the series of $\log\frac{1+x}{1-x}$ at $x=\delta/(2+\delta)$) and $(1-\delta)\log(1-\delta)\ge-\delta+\delta^2/2$.

nodes.name: Lower tails, MGF and parametric Chernoff bounds
nodes.statement: Let $X=\sum_{i<n}Y_i(\omega_i)$ with independent uniform $\{0,1\}$-valued coordinates and $\mu=\E X$. Then $\Pr(X\le\E X-\lambda)\le e^{-2\lambda^2/n}$, and a $\{0,1\}$ coordinate has variance at most its mean. For every real $t$, $\E e^{tX}\le\exp(\mu(e^t-1))$; hence $\Pr(X\ge k)\le\exp(\mu(e^t-1)-tk)$ for $t\ge0$ and $\Pr(X\le k)\le\exp(\mu(e^t-1)-tk)$ for $t\le0$. If $\E X\le\mu\le k$ with $\mu>0$, then $\Pr(X\ge k)\le\exp(k-\mu-k\log(k/\mu))$; if $0<k\le\mu\le\E X$, then $\Pr(X\le k)\le\exp(k-\mu-k\log(k/\mu))$. Finally $\Pr(X\le(1-\delta)\E X)\le\exp(-\delta^2\E X/2)$ for $0\le\delta<1$.
nodes.label: thm:chernoffmgf

nodes.statement: The lower Hoeffding tail is the upper one for $1-Y_i$. For the MGF bound, $e^{tY}=1+(e^t-1)Y$ on $\{0,1\}$ and $1+y\le e^y$, factor by factor; Markov's inequality applied to $e^{tX}$ gives the tails, and $t=\log(k/\mu)$ the closed forms (the exponent is monotone in $\mu$ in the right direction). The last bound is the lower bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:chernoff} with $\mu_L=\E X$ (trivial for $\delta=0$).

nodes.name: Elementary tail bounds and monotonicity
nodes.statement: Probability is monotone in the event. An observable $f\le1$ with $f(b)<1$ at a point of positive weight has expectation $<1$. Markov's inequality $\Pr(X\ge c)\le\E X/c$ for $X\ge0$, $c>0$; in particular $\Pr(\sum_iY_i(\omega_i)\ge1)\le\sum_i\E Y_i$ for nonnegative coordinates. One round of $\mathrm{step}$ lands in an event with probability at least $1-\E[\mathrm{bad}]$ when $\mathrm{bad}\ge0$ is at least $1$ on every miss. If $f\le Kf$, then $n\mapsto K^nf(a)$ is nondecreasing; in particular the occupation probability of an absorbing event is nondecreasing in time. Finally $e^{-2\log n}=1/n^2$ for $n\ge1$, and $\log n>0$ forces $n\ge1$.
nodes.label: lem:tail

nodes.statement: Pointwise comparisons of indicators, integrated by monotonicity of the expectation; for the kernel statements, induction on time with $K^{n+1}f=K^n(Kf)$.

nodes.name: Nested phases
nodes.statement: Let $A_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq A_T$ be sets of states such that from $A_i$ the chain stays in $A_i$ with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$ and, for $i<T$, enters $A_{i+1}$ with probability at least $1-\nu$. From $A_1$, after $\ell T$ steps the chain is in $A_T$ with probability at least $1-T(\ell\varepsilon+\nu^\ell)$.
nodes.label: thm:phases

nodes.statement: Track the indicator of lying outside a set. In $\ell$ steps the chain leaves $A_i$ with probability at most $\ell\varepsilon$, and misses $A_{i+1}$ in all $\ell$ steps with probability at most $\nu^\ell$. Sum over the $T$ phases.

nodes.name: Time-dependent chain
nodes.statement: A family of kernels $(K_t)_{t\ge0}$ moves the chain from time $t$ to time $t+1$ with $K_t$; $\mathrm{iterateSeq}(K,n,f)(a)$ is the expectation of $f$ at time $n$ from $a$. A constant family gives the iterates of a single kernel.
nodes.label: def:iterateseq

nodes.statement: Induction on $n$.

nodes.name: Drift lemma; Berenbrink et al., ICALP 2016, Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Let $\Psi\ge0$, and for $t<T$ let $c_t\ge0$, $\E[\Psi(X_{t+1})\mid X_t=x]\le\Psi(x)-c_t/\Psi(x)$ when $\Psi(x)>0$, and $\E[\Psi(X_{t+1})\mid X_t=x]=0$ when $\Psi(x)=0$. If $\sum_{t<T}c_t\ge4\Psi(x_0)^2$, then $\Pr_{x_0}(\Psi(X_T)=0)\ge1/2$.
nodes.label: thm:drift

nodes.statement: Let $q=\Pr(\Psi(X_T)>0)$; survival is nonincreasing, so it is at least $q$ before $T$. With $\lambda=q/\Psi(x_0)$, the bound $1/y\ge2\lambda-\lambda^2y$ linearizes the drift: $\E\Psi(X_{t+1})\le(1+c_t\lambda^2)\E\Psi(X_t) -2c_t\lambda\Pr(\Psi(X_t)>0)\le\E\Psi(X_t)-c_t\lambda q$. (The paper uses Jensen's inequality here; this is its optimal-$\lambda$ form.) Summing, $0<m q\le\E\Psi(X_T)\le\Psi(x_0)(1-4q^2)$ if $q>0$, where $m>0$ is the least positive value of $\Psi$; hence $q\le1/2$.

nodes.name: Multiplicative drift; the argument of Lemma 2.4 there
nodes.statement: Let $\Psi\ge0$ with every positive value at least $\Psi_{\min}>0$, and $\E[\Psi(X_{t+1})\mid X_t=x]\le(1-\delta_t)\Psi(x)$ for all $x$ and $t<T$. Then $\Pr_{x_0}(\Psi(X_T)>0)\le\prod_{t<T}(1-\delta_t)\,\Psi(x_0)/\Psi_{\min}$.
nodes.label: thm:multdrift

nodes.statement: By induction $\E\Psi(X_T)\le\prod_{t<T}(1-\delta_t)\Psi(x_0)$ (the factors are nonnegative unless $\Psi\equiv0$); then Markov's inequality $\mathbf 1_{\Psi>0}\le\Psi/\Psi_{\min}$.

nodes.name: Synchronous neighbour rounds
nodes.statement: In a round $r\in\prod_vN(v)$ every vertex picks a neighbour. Under the uniform distribution the picks are independent and uniform: $\E\prod_vf_v(r_v)=\prod_v\E_{u\in N(v)}f_v(u)$, and, without isolated vertices, $\E g(r_v)=\E_{u\in N(v)}g(u)$. A uniform vertex $v$ with a uniform round gives the sequential step ``uniform vertex, uniform neighbour $r_v$''.
nodes.label: lem:neighborround

nodes.statement: $\sum_r\prod_vf_v(r_v)=\prod_v\sum_{u\in N(v)}f_v(u)$ and $|\prod_vN(v)|=\prod_v\deg v$; the marginals take $f_w=1$ for $w\ne v$.

nodes.name: Uniform oriented edge
nodes.statement: For a uniform dart $d$ of $G$, $\E F(d_1,d_2)=\sum_v\sum_{u\in N(v)}F(v,u)/(2|E|)$; reversing $d$ preserves the law, its underlying edge is a uniform edge, and its tail is $v$ with probability $\deg v/(2|E|)$.
nodes.label: lem:edgeround

nodes.statement: Group the darts by tail (the darts with tail $v$ are the neighbours of $v$) or by edge (each edge carries two darts).

nodes.name: Hitting probability
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{hitProb}(K,B,n)(a)=\Pr_a(\exists s\le n,\ X_s\in B)=\Pr_a(T_B\le n)$, the expectation over the first $n$ transitions of the indicator that one of the states at the times $0,\dots,n$ lies in $B$.
nodes.label: def:hitprob

nodes.name: Geometric drift bound for hitting times
nodes.statement: Let $V\ge0$ vanish on $B$ and be at least $V_{\min}>0$ off $B$, with $\E[V(X_{t+1})\mid X_t=x]\le\rho V(x)$ for $x\notin B$. Then $\Pr_a(T_B>t)\le\rho^tV(a)/V_{\min}$.
nodes.label: lem:hitdrift

nodes.statement: In the chain stopped on entering $B$, being outside $B$ at time $t$ is the event $T_B>t$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:multdrift} to the stopped chain with $\delta=1-\rho$.

nodes.name: Hitting-time bound; Doerr, Goldberg, Minder, Sauerwald, Scheideler, SPAA 2011, Claim 2.9
nodes.statement: Let $c_1>1$ and $c_2,c_3,c_4,c_6>0$. There is $c_5>0$ such that for every finite chain and observable $X\in\{0,\dots,q\}$ with $c_4\log q\le q$: if from every state below the target $\Pr[X_{t+1}\ge\min\{c_1X_t,q\}]\ge 1-e^{-c_2X_t}$, and $\Pr[X_{t+1}\ge1]\ge c_3$ when $X_t=0$, then $X$ reaches $c_4\log q$ within $c_5\log q+\log_{c_1}(c_4\log q)$ steps with probability at least $1-q^{-c_6}$ (equivalently within $C\log q$ steps).
nodes.label: thm:drifthitting

nodes.statement: The paper omits the proof. Let $p=\min\{c_3,1-e^{-c_2}\}$, $\theta=1/p$ and $\beta=c_2/2$. For a large threshold $x_0$ take $g(x)=1-\eta(\theta^x-1)$ for $x\le x_0$, with $\eta$ chosen so that $g(x_0)=1/2$, and $g(x)=\tfrac12e^{-\beta(x-x_0)}$ for $x\ge x_0$; let $V=g(X)$ below the target and $V=0$ on it. Below $x_0$ a step goes up by at least one with probability at least $p$, and $pg(x+1)+1-p\le\rho g(x)$ with $\rho=1-(1-p)\eta/2$; above $x_0$ growth by $c_1$ fails with probability at most $e^{-c_2x}$, and the expected potential is at most $\tfrac38e^{-\beta(x-x_0)}\le\rho g(x)$. Since $V\le1$ and $V\ge\tfrac12q^{-\beta c_4}$ below the target, Lemma~\ref{lem:hitdrift} gives $\Pr(T>t)\le2\rho^tq^{\beta c_4}\le q^{-c_6}$ for $t\ge(1+\beta c_4+c_6)\log q/\log(1/\rho)$.

nodes.name: Percolated graph and epidemic
nodes.statement: Every edge $e$ of a finite graph $G$ carries a coin $\omega(e)\in\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$; the percolated graph $G_\omega$ keeps the edges whose coin is true. In one round, a susceptible node becomes infected if it has an infected neighbour across an open edge, and every infected node recovers. Initially the set $I_0$ is infected and nobody is recovered. We write $d(v)\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ for the distance from $I_0$ to $v$ in $G_\omega$.
nodes.label: def:reedfrost

nodes.name: Distance facts
nodes.statement: $d(v)=0$ iff $v\in I_0$; if $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G_\omega$ then $d(v)\le d(u)+1$; if $d(v)=t+1$ then $v$ has a neighbour $u$ in $G_\omega$ with $d(u)=t$; $d(v)<\infty$ iff $v$ is connected to $I_0$ in $G_\omega$, and then $d(v)<|V|$.
nodes.label: lem:dist

nodes.statement: The infimum over $I_0$ is attained; take the second-to-last vertex of a shortest walk; a shortest walk is a path.

nodes.name: Infected and recovered sets
nodes.statement: For every coin assignment and every $t$, the nodes infected in round $t$ are those with $d(v)=t$, and the nodes recovered by round $t$ are those with $d(v)<t$.
nodes.label: thm:layers

nodes.statement: Both statements together, by induction on $t$, using Lemma~\ref{lem:dist}.

nodes.name: Extinction and final size
nodes.statement: Nobody is infected in round $t$ as soon as every finite $d(v)$ is $<t$, in particular for $t\ge|V|$; the nodes recovered after $|V|$ rounds are those connected to $I_0$ in $G_\omega$.
nodes.label: cor:final

nodes.statement: Immediate from Theorem~\ref{thm:layers} and $d(v)<|V|$ when finite.

nodes.name: Reed--Frost $\Leftrightarrow$ bond percolation
nodes.statement: With independent Bernoulli$(p)$ coins, each edge is open with probability $p$, and the probability that $v$ is eventually infected equals the probability that $v$ is connected to $I_0$ by open edges.
nodes.label: thm:perc

nodes.statement: The two events coincide for every coin assignment (Corollary~\ref{cor:final}).

nodes.name: Binomial tail and Chernoff bound
nodes.statement: At least $t$ successes among $t(d-1)+1$ independent Bernoulli$(p)$ trials occur with probability at most $\exp(\varepsilon - \varepsilon^2 t/2)$.
nodes.label: lem:chernoff

nodes.statement: Markov's inequality on $e^{\varepsilon X}$ and the bound $\mathbb E[e^{\varepsilon X}] \le \exp(\mu(e^{\varepsilon}-1))$ for a sum of independent trials with mean $\mu \le (1-\varepsilon)(t+1)$ (the Chernoff layer of the shared \texttt{dynamics} package, before optimizing the tilt: \texttt{Distribution.prob\_ge\_le\_exp}), then $(1-\varepsilon)e^{\varepsilon} \le 1 - \varepsilon^2/2$.

nodes.name: Deferred decisions
nodes.statement: The component of $s$ in $G_p$ has more than $t$ vertices with probability at most that of at least $t$ successes in $t(d-1)+1$ independent Bernoulli$(p)$ trials.
nodes.label: thm:deferred

nodes.statement: For an exploration state (discovered set $D$, examined pairs $X$, forced closed), induction on a budget $m \ge \mathrm{frontier}(D, X) + (k-1)(d-1)$: conditioning on the coin of one frontier edge, a closed coin removes that edge from the frontier, and an open one adds a vertex and at most $d-1$ new frontier edges at it while removing the examined one. This is the recursion of the binomial tail. The initial frontier of $\{s\}$ has at most $d$ edges.

nodes.name: Theorems E.1 and 2.3
nodes.statement: The component of any vertex has more than $t$ vertices with probability at most $\exp(\varepsilon - \varepsilon^2 t/2)$, and with probability at least $1 - 1/n$ every component of $G_p$ has at most $(10/\varepsilon^2)\log n$ vertices.
nodes.label: thm:subcritical

nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:deferred} and Lemma~\ref{lem:chernoff}, then a union bound over the vertices.

nodes.name: Subcritical Reed--Frost and Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi
nodes.statement: With probability at least $1 - 1/n$, the Reed--Frost epidemic with $R_0 = p(d-1) \le 1 - \varepsilon$ infects at most $|I_0| (10/\varepsilon^2)\log n$ nodes and nobody is infected in round $\lfloor (10/\varepsilon^2)\log n \rfloor$; and every component of $G(n, c/n)$ with $c \le 1 - \varepsilon$ has at most $(10/\varepsilon^2)\log n$ vertices.
nodes.label: cor:subcritical

nodes.statement: The final outbreak is the union of the components of $I_0$, and distances inside a component are smaller than its size (Corollary~\ref{cor:final}). $G(n, c/n)$ is bond percolation on $K_n$, with $d = n - 1$ and $p(d-1) \le c$.

nodes.name: Small-world graphs and the threshold
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{SWG}(n, q)$ is $C_n \cup \mathrm{perc}(K_n, b)$ with $b$ i.i.d.\ Bernoulli$(q)$, and $3\text{-}\mathrm{SWG}(n)$ is $C_n \cup M$ with $M$ uniform among the perfect matchings of $K_n$ ($n$ even). The critical value $p^* = (\sqrt{c^2+6c+1} - c - 1)/(2c)$ is the root of $c p (1 + p) = 1 - p$, so that $p < p^*$ if and only if $c p(1+p) < 1-p$; for $c = 1$, $p^* = \sqrt 2 - 1$. The graph $3\text{-}\mathrm{SWG}(n)$ has maximum degree $3$.
nodes.label: def:swg

nodes.name: Collapsing the two coin families
nodes.statement: The percolation graph of $\mathrm{SWG}(n, q)$ with parameter $p$ has the law of the percolation of $K_n$ with independent coins, of probability $p$ on the cycle edges and $pq$ on the other pairs.
nodes.label: lem:swg-collapse

nodes.statement: A pair is an open edge if and only if its percolation coin is open and it is a cycle edge or an open bridge; these combined coins are independent across pairs, with the stated probabilities.

nodes.name: Supermartingale for adaptive observations
nodes.statement: If an adaptive process reads, at each step, coordinates of an independent family not read before, and every factor $f_h \ge 0$ satisfies $\mathbb E[f_h(\mathrm{obs}_h)] \le 1$ for every history $h$, then the product of the factors along the process has expectation at most $1$.
nodes.label: lem:swg-mart

nodes.statement: Condition on the history: the event that the history is $h$ depends only on the coordinates read along $h$, which are independent of the fresh ones (principle of deferred decisions); induction on the number of steps.

nodes.name: Weighted exploration
nodes.statement: Explore the cluster of $s$ one node at a time, with independent Bernoulli$(r_e)$ coins, giving each discovered node the weight $h_e \in [w_{\min}, w_{\max}]$ of the pair through which it was discovered. If the expected weight discovered from every node of weight $w$ is at most $\lambda w$, then for $\theta \ge 0$ and $\kappa \le 2$ with $\theta w_{\max} \le \kappa - 1$ and $\kappa\lambda \le 1$, the cluster of $s$ has more than $t$ nodes with probability at most $\exp(-\theta((1-\kappa\lambda) t w_{\min} - w_{\max}))$.
nodes.label: thm:swg-explore

nodes.statement: The exponential of $\theta$ times (discovered weight $-\ \kappa\lambda\,\cdot$ processed weight) is a supermartingale, by $1 - r + r e^x \le e^{\kappa r x}$ for $0 \le x \le \kappa - 1 \le 1$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:swg-mart}. A cluster with more than $t$ nodes leaves $t$ processed and $t + 1$ discovered nodes after $t$ steps; Markov's inequality concludes.

nodes.name: Lemma C.1 and Theorem 2.1, claim 2
nodes.statement: Let $c > 0$, $p_0 = p^* - \varepsilon > 0$ and $\delta = 1 - p_0 - c p_0 (1 + p_0)$. For $n \ge 2$, $q = c/n$ and $p \le p_0$, with probability at least $1 - 2/n$ every component of the percolated $\mathrm{SWG}(n, q)$ has at most $(64/\delta^2) \log n$ nodes.
nodes.label: thm:swg-sub

nodes.statement: Weights $1$ (discovered through a cycle edge: at most one undiscovered cycle neighbour) and $1 + p_0$ (otherwise: at most two), and at most $n$ further pairs each open with probability $pc/n$: the expected discovered weight is at most $(1 - \delta/2)$ times the weight. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:swg-explore} with $\theta = \delta/8$, $\kappa = 1 + \delta/4$ and a union bound over the nodes.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2, claim 2
nodes.statement: For $p < 1/2 - \varepsilon$, with probability at least $1 - 1/n$ every component of the percolated $3\text{-}\mathrm{SWG}(n)$ has at most $(10/(2\varepsilon)^2) \log n$ nodes.
nodes.label: cor:swg3-sub

nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:subcritical} with $d = 3$ and $2\varepsilon$ in place of $\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Theorems 2.4 and 2.5, claim 2
nodes.statement: Below the threshold ($p < p^* - \varepsilon$ on $\mathrm{SWG}(n, c/n)$, $p < 1/2 - \varepsilon$ on $3\text{-}\mathrm{SWG}(n)$), with probability at least $1 - C/n$ the Reed--Frost epidemic from $I_0$ is over within $\beta \log n$ rounds and at most $\beta |I_0| \log n$ nodes are recovered at the end.
nodes.label: cor:swg-rf

nodes.statement: Deterministic consequences of the component bounds (Corollary~\ref{cor:subcritical}).

nodes.name: Principle of deferred decisions
nodes.statement: If an adaptive strategy queries the coins one at a time, the next coordinate being a function of the answers so far, and never queries a coordinate twice among its first $m$ queries, then its first $m$ answers are i.i.d.\ Bernoulli$(p)$.
nodes.label: lem:deferred

nodes.statement: The answers equal a list $L$ iff the coordinates queried along $L$, which are determined by $L$ and distinct, take the values of $L$: a cylinder event of probability $\prod_k w(L_k)$.

nodes.name: Depth-first search fed with answers
nodes.statement: The search of Krivelevich--Sudakov (Section~2) with the sets $S$ (done), $U$ (stack) and $T$ (unvisited), stopped before each query; after $U=T=\emptyset$ the remaining pairs are queried.
nodes.label: def:dfs

nodes.name: Properties of the search
nodes.statement: Every pair is queried at most once; all pairs between $S$ and $T$ have been queried negatively; $U$ spans a path; $|U|\le 1+\sum X_i$ and, while $T\ne\emptyset$, $|S\cup U|\ge\sum X_i$; the vertices of one epoch are connected; when an epoch starts, the explored set $D$ has all its pairs with $V\setminus D$ queried.
nodes.label: lem:dfs

nodes.statement: An invariant preserved by every move and answer; moves without query terminate because $2|S|+|U|\le 2n$ increases.

nodes.name: Deterministic analysis
nodes.statement: The deterministic steps of the proofs of Theorems~1 and~2 of the paper: $|S\cup U|<n/3$ at time $N_0$, $|U|\ge \ell n+1$, and the current epoch started before $t_1$.
nodes.label: lem:analysis

nodes.statement: In each case $|S||T|$ (or $|D|(n-|D|)$) would exceed the number of queries.

nodes.name: Krivelevich--Sudakov, Lemma~1(2), with Chernoff
nodes.statement: Among $N_0$ i.i.d.\ Bernoulli$(p)$ trials, the number of successes deviates from $N_0p$ by $\delta N_0p$ with probability at most $2e^{-\delta^2N_0p/3}$ (Chernoff bounds of FND-3 instead of Chebyshev, as in the paper's Discussion, item~1); the same holds at every time of a window.
nodes.label: lem:ks1

nodes.statement: Chernoff bounds and the union bound.

nodes.name: Long path; Theorem~1(2)
nodes.statement: For every small enough $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C$ such that $G(n,(1+\varepsilon)/n)$ contains a path with at least $\varepsilon^2n/5$ edges with probability at least $1-C/n$.
nodes.label: thm:path

nodes.statement: Run the search for $N_0=\lfloor\varepsilon n^2/2\rfloor$ queries; on the typical event the stack is a path of the required length.

nodes.name: Giant component; Theorem~2 and every $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: For every small enough $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C$ such that $G(n,(1+\varepsilon)/n)$ has a component with at least $\varepsilon n/2$ vertices with probability at least $1-C/n$; for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $c>0$ and $C$ such that it has a component with at least $cn$ vertices with probability at least $1-C/n$.
nodes.label: thm:giant

nodes.statement: No epoch starts between the times $t_1=\lfloor\eta n^2\rfloor$ and $N_0=\lfloor\theta n^2\rfloor$, so the positive answers in between lie in one component; $\theta=\varepsilon/2$ for the first statement, $\theta$ small in terms of $\varepsilon$ for the second.

nodes.name: Supercritical Reed--Frost epidemics
nodes.statement: On $K_n$ with $pn=R_0>1$, the Reed--Frost epidemic started from any single node infects at least $cn$ nodes with probability at least $q>0$ for $n\ge n_0$; for $R_0=1+\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon$ small, at least $\varepsilon n/2$ nodes with probability at least $\varepsilon/2-C/n$.
nodes.label: cor:outbreak

nodes.statement: The final outbreak is the component of the initial node (Corollary~\ref{cor:final}); by symmetry of $K_n$ this node lies in a component of size $\ge k$ with probability at least $k/n$ times the probability that such a component exists.

nodes.name: Solutions
nodes.statement: Let $\beta,\gamma>0$ and $R_0=\beta/\gamma$. A solution is a triple $(s,i,r)$ of real functions such that $t\mapsto(s,i,r)(t)$ is an integral curve on $[0,\infty)$ (one-sided derivative at $0$) of the field $(s,i,r)\mapsto(-\beta si,\ \beta si-\gamma i,\ \gamma i)$, with $s(0),i(0)>0$, $r(0)=0$ and $s(0)+i(0)+r(0)=1$. Solutions are assumed, not constructed.
nodes.label: def:km

nodes.name: Invariants
nodes.statement: On $[0,\infty)$: $s+i+r=1$; $s,i>0$ and $r\ge0$; $s$ is strictly decreasing and $r$ strictly increasing; and $s(t)=s(0)e^{-R_0r(t)}$.
nodes.label: thm:km-basic

nodes.statement: The derivatives of $s+i+r$ and of $se^{R_0r}$ vanish ($R_0\gamma=\beta$), and a function with zero right derivative is constant. For $i>0$, compare $i$ with the barrier $b(t)=\tfrac{i(0)}2e^{-\gamma t}$: where they touch, $b'=-\gamma i<\beta si-\gamma i=i'$ since $s>0$, so $i\ge b$. Monotonicity follows from the signs of $s'=-\beta si$ and $r'=\gamma i$.

nodes.name: Threshold
nodes.statement: If $R_0s(0)\le1$, then $i$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,\infty)$. The function $i$ is strictly increasing on some $[0,\varepsilon]$, $\varepsilon>0$, iff $R_0s(0)>1$.
nodes.label: thm:km-threshold

nodes.statement: $i'=i(\beta s-\gamma)$ and $s(t)<s(0)$ for $t>0$. If $R_0s(0)>1$, then $\beta s-\gamma>0$ near $0$ by continuity.

nodes.name: Limits and final size
nodes.statement: $i(t)\to0$, $s(t)\to s_\infty$ and $r(t)\to1-s_\infty$; moreover $s_\infty=s(0)e^{-R_0(1-s_\infty)}$, $0<s_\infty<1/R_0$, and $s_\infty$ is the unique root of this equation in $(0,1/R_0]$ and in $(0,1]$.
nodes.label: thm:km-final

nodes.statement: $s$ and $r$ are monotone and bounded, so $i=1-s-r$ converges; if $i\to L>0$, the mean value theorem makes $r$ grow by more than $1$. Pass to the limit in $s=s(0)e^{-R_0r}$. If $R_0s_\infty\ge1$ then $i'>0$ forever, contradicting $i\to0$. Uniqueness: $\log x-R_0x$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1/R_0]$ and strictly decreasing on $[1/R_0,\infty)$, and at $x=1$ it exceeds its value $\log s(0)-R_0$ at the roots because $s(0)<1$.

nodes.name: Peak
nodes.statement: If $R_0s(0)>1$, there is $t_{\max}>0$ with $s(t_{\max})=1/R_0$ such that $i$ is strictly increasing on $[0,t_{\max}]$ and strictly decreasing on $[t_{\max},\infty)$, and $i(t_{\max})=i(0)+s(0)-1/R_0-\log(R_0s(0))/R_0$.
nodes.label: thm:km-peak

nodes.statement: Intermediate value theorem between $s(0)>1/R_0$ and $s_\infty<1/R_0$; the sign of $\beta s-\gamma$ changes at $t_{\max}$. The value follows from $\log s=\log s(0)-R_0r$ and $r=1-s-i$.

nodes.name: The uniformized SIR chain
nodes.statement: Let $\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb N$. A configuration assigns to each of $N$ agents a compartment $S$, $I$ or $R$; $X=(S,I,R)/N$ are the scaled counts. One step draws $(u,v)$ uniformly in $[N]^2$ and one of $\beta+\gamma$ equally likely clocks: on one of the $\beta$ infection clocks an infected $u$ infects a susceptible $v$, on one of the $\gamma$ recovery clocks an infected $u$ recovers. This is the continuous-time chain ($S+I\to2I$ at rate $\beta SI/N$, $I\to R$ at rate $\gamma I$) uniformized at rate $(\beta+\gamma)N$. The deviation probability is the probability that $\|X_k-x(k/((\beta+\gamma)N))\|_\infty>\theta$ for some $k\le n$.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time
nodes.label: def:kurtz

nodes.name: Drift and bounded increments
nodes.statement: $\mathbb E[X_{k+1}-X_k\mid X_k=x]=F(x)/((\beta+\gamma)N)$ with $F$ the Kermack--McKendrick field, and $\|X_{k+1}-X_k\|_\infty\le1/N$.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time
nodes.label: lem:kurtz-drift

nodes.statement: Among the $N^2(\beta+\gamma)$ rounds, $\beta IS$ move an agent from $S$ to $I$ and $\gamma NI$ move one from $I$ to $R$; a round changes the compartment of at most one agent.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time

nodes.name: Maximal Azuma--Hoeffding
nodes.statement: If increments $D(X_j,\rho_j)$ along i.i.d.\ uniform rounds have zero conditional mean and $|D|\le c$, their partial sums $M_k$ satisfy $\mathbb P(\exists k\le n,\ M_k\ge\lambda)\le e^{-\lambda^2/(2nc^2)}$.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time
nodes.label: lem:azuma

nodes.statement: Hoeffding's lemma ($\mathbb E e^{\theta D}\le\cosh(\theta c)\le e^{\theta^2c^2/2}$ by convexity) makes $e^{\theta M_k-k\theta^2c^2/2}$ a nonnegative supermartingale; Ville's maximal inequality, proved by induction on $n$ peeling off the first round, bounds the probability that it reaches $\mu$ by $1/\mu$; take $\theta=\lambda/(nc^2)$.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time

nodes.name: Law of large numbers
nodes.statement: Let $\beta,\gamma,T>0$. There are $C,c>0$ and $L$ such that for every $N$, every initial configuration, every solution $x$ of the Kermack--McKendrick system started in the simplex and every $\varepsilon>0$, with probability at least $1-Ce^{-c\varepsilon^2N}$, $\|X_k-x(k/((\beta+\gamma)N))\|_\infty\le L\|X_0-x(0)\|_\infty+\varepsilon$ for all $k\le T(\beta+\gamma)N$. Hence, if $X_0\to x(0)$, the scaled chain converges to $x$ in probability, uniformly on $[0,T]$.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time
nodes.label: thm:kurtz

nodes.statement: The simplex is invariant under the ODE (first integral for $s$, integrating factor for $i$); there $F$ is $(2\beta+\gamma)$-Lipschitz and bounded by $\beta+\gamma$, so one Euler step errs by $O(h^2)$, $h=1/((\beta+\gamma)N)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:kurtz-drift} each coordinate of $X_k-X_0-h\sum_{j<k}F(X_j)$ is a martingale with increments at most $2/N$; on the event where the six one-sided maximal deviations stay below $\delta=\varepsilon/(2L)$, the discrete Gr\"onwall inequality gives the bound with $L=e^{(2\beta+\gamma)T}$, once $\varepsilon N\ge2LT(2\beta+\gamma)$; Lemma~\ref{lem:azuma} bounds the complement by $6e^{-c\varepsilon^2N}$. Small $N$ and $\varepsilon\ge2$ are absorbed in $C$.
nodes.section: 40 Kurtz's law of large numbers for SIR, in discrete time

nodes.name: Rumor-spreading processes
nodes.statement: A rumor-spreading process on $n$ nodes is a Markov kernel on the set $S$ of informed nodes under which informed nodes stay informed. For a round started from $S$, $\mathrm{informProb}(S,x)$ is the probability that $x$ is informed after the round and $\mathrm{cov}(S,x,y)$ the covariance of the events that $x$ and $y$ are. The tail of the spreading time is $\mathrm{notYet}(m,t,S)=\Pr[\text{fewer than }m\text{ nodes informed after }t\text{ rounds from }S]=\Pr[T(|S|,m)>t]$; expected times are bounded through all partial sums of $\sum_t\Pr[T>t]$. Homogeneity (Definition~6) is defined but not assumed.
nodes.label: def:rumor-process

nodes.name: Upper growth and shrinking conditions
nodes.statement: Upper exponential growth (Definition~9): for $1\le|S|=k<fn$, every uninformed node is informed with probability at least $\gamma\frac kn(1-a\frac kn-\frac b{\ln n})$ and covariances are at most $ck/n^2$. Upper exponential shrinking (Definition~11): when $u=n-|S|\le gn$, every uninformed node stays uninformed with probability at most $e^{-\rho}+au/n$ and covariances are at most $c/u$.
nodes.label: def:rumor-conditions

nodes.name: Lemma 9
nodes.statement: If distinct uninformed nodes have covariance at most $c$, the number of informed nodes after one round has variance at most its expected increase plus $c(n-|S|)^2$.
nodes.label: lem:rumor-variance

nodes.statement: Expand the variance of a sum of indicators.

nodes.name: Lemma 19
nodes.statement: If every uninformed node is informed with probability at least $p$ in every round started with $\ell\le|S|<m$ informed nodes, then $\Pr[T(\ell,m)>r]\le\frac{n-\ell}{n-m}(1-p)^r$ and $E[T(\ell,m)]\le\frac{n-\ell}{n-m}\cdot\frac1p$.
nodes.label: lem:rumor-connect

nodes.statement: The potential $n-|S|$ (set to $0$ once $|S|\ge m$) contracts by $1-p$ in expectation.

nodes.name: Theorem 21: exponential growth
nodes.statement: Under the upper exponential growth conditions, with $\gamma$ between two positive constants and $af<1$, from any nonempty $S$: $\Pr[T(|S|,fn)>\lceil\log_{1+\gamma}n\rceil+r]\le Ae^{-\alpha r}$ and $E[T(|S|,fn)]\le\log_{1+\gamma}n+B$, with constants depending only on the parameters.
nodes.label: thm:rumor-growth

nodes.statement: Phases $k_{j+1}=k_j+E_0(k_j)$ with a round target $E_0(k)=E(k)-Ak^{3/4}$; Cantelli's inequality (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-variance}) bounds the probability of missing a target, and a phase potential on the iterated kernel replaces the paper's domination by geometric variables. Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-connect} crosses the last stretch up to $fn$.

nodes.name: Lemma 20, corrected
nodes.statement: If every round started with $1\le|S|<fn$ has $p_k\le p$ and covariances at most $c/n$, then (one round) for every $f'\in\,]f+p(1-f),1[$, a round from $|S|<fn$ ends with at least $f'n$ informed nodes with probability at most $C/n$; and (path form) there is $f'\in\,]f,1[$ such that the probability of jumping over $[fn,f'n[$ within $t$ rounds is at most $\frac Cn$ times the expected number of these rounds started below $fn$, i.e.\ $O(E[T(|S|,fn)]/n)$.
nodes.label: lem:rumor-jump

nodes.statement: Chebyshev's inequality with Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-variance} for one round, then a union bound over the rounds along the trajectory.

nodes.name: Theorem 31: exponential shrinking
nodes.statement: Under the upper exponential shrinking conditions, with $\rho$ between two positive constants and $e^{-\rho_{lo}}+ag<1$, from any $S$ with $n-|S|\le gn$: $\Pr[T(|S|,n)>\lceil\ln n/\rho\rceil+r]\le Ae^{-\alpha r}$ and $E[T(|S|,n)]\le\ln n/\rho+B$.
nodes.label: thm:rumor-shrinking

nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-connect} first brings the number $u$ of uninformed nodes below $g_0n$; then the potential $\Phi=u+\frac\beta nu^2$ satisfies $E[\Phi']\le e^{-\rho}(1+K/n)\Phi$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-variance} for the second moment), which replaces the paper's phase calculus.

nodes.name: Total spreading time
nodes.statement: Under the growth conditions on $[1,fn[$, the shrinking conditions below $gn$ uninformed nodes and a probability at least $p>0$ of being informed in between, from any nonempty $S$: $\Pr[T>\lceil\log_{1+\gamma}n\rceil+\lceil\ln n/\rho\rceil+r]\le Ae^{-\alpha r}$ and $E[T]\le\log_{1+\gamma}n+\ln n/\rho+B$.
nodes.label: thm:rumor-total

nodes.statement: Compose the three exponential tails (Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-growth}, Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-connect}, Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-shrinking}) by the Markov property at fixed times, and sum the tail.

nodes.name: Upper double exponential shrinking conditions
nodes.statement: Definition~13: when $n^{1-\alpha}\le u=n-|S|\le gn$, every uninformed node stays uninformed with probability at most $a(u/n)^{\ell-1}$ and covariances are at most $cn/u^2$. Fast finishing (the second hypothesis of Theorem~43): when $u\le n^{1-\alpha}$, every uninformed node stays uninformed with probability at most $n^{-\tau}$.
nodes.label: def:rumor-double

nodes.name: Theorem 43: double exponential shrinking
nodes.statement: Let $\ell>1$, $a,c\ge0$, $g,\alpha\in[0,1]$, $ag^{\ell-1}<1$ and $\tau>0$. Under the upper double exponential shrinking conditions and fast finishing, from any $S$ with $n-|S|\le gn$: $\Pr[T(|S|,n)>\lceil\log_\ell\ln n\rceil+r]\le Cn^{A'-\alpha'r}$ and $E[T(|S|,n)]\le\log_\ell\ln n+B$.
nodes.label: thm:rumor-double

nodes.statement: Three stages. Geometric targets $g\mu^jn$, $\mu=(1+ag^{\ell-1})/2$, bring $u$ below $g_0n$ in a constant number of phases; double exponential targets $\varepsilon_{j+1}=2a_1\varepsilon_j^\ell$, i.e.\ $\varepsilon_j=e^{-(\kappa+\ell^jD_0)}$, bring it below $\varepsilon_Jn\le n^{1-\beta/(2\ell)}$ in $J\le\log_\ell\ln n$ phases; below that, every uninformed node stays uninformed with probability at most $n^{-\tau_3}$ and Markov's inequality finishes. A phase fails with probability at most $n^{-2\delta}$ (Chebyshev with Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-variance} above $n^{1-\alpha}$ uninformed nodes, Markov with fast finishing below), and the phase potential $\lambda^{J-j}$, $\lambda=n^\delta$, contracts by $n^{-2\delta}+n^{-\delta}$ per round. The paper's first stage uses Lemma~19, whose tail rate does not depend on $n$; the per-round Chebyshev bound gives the polynomial tail.

nodes.name: Total spreading time, double exponential shrinking
nodes.statement: Under the growth conditions on $[1,fn[$, the double exponential shrinking conditions and fast finishing below $gn$ uninformed nodes ($g>0$), and a probability at least $p>0$ of being informed in between, from any nonempty $S$: $\Pr[T>\lceil\log_{1+\gamma}n\rceil+\lceil\log_\ell\ln n\rceil+r]\le Ae^{-\kappa r}$ and $E[T]\le\log_{1+\gamma}n+\log_\ell\ln n+B$.
nodes.label: thm:rumor-total-double

nodes.statement: As Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-total}, with Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-double} in the last stage (its polynomial tail is an exponential tail once $\ln n\ge1$).

nodes.name: Push, pull and push--pull on $K_n$
nodes.statement: In a round every node calls a uniformly random node (itself included), independently. Push: informed nodes inform the nodes they call. Pull: uninformed nodes calling an informed node become informed. Push--pull: both.
nodes.label: def:rumor-protocols

nodes.name: One-round quantities and conditions
nodes.statement: With $k=|S|$ informed nodes, an uninformed node is informed with probability $1-(1-\frac1n)^k$ (push), $\frac kn$ (pull), $1-(1-\frac1n)^k(1-\frac kn)$ (push--pull); distinct uninformed nodes are nonpositively correlated (independent for pull). Hence push satisfies the upper growth conditions with $\gamma=1$, $a=\frac12$ and the upper shrinking conditions with $\rho=1$, $a=\frac2e$, $g=\frac12$; pull and push--pull satisfy the growth conditions with $\gamma=1$, $a=0$ and $\gamma=2$, $a=\frac34$, and the double exponential shrinking conditions with $\ell=2$, $a=1$, $g=\alpha=\frac12$ and fast finishing with $\tau=\frac12$ (all with $b=c=0$, $f=\frac12$).
nodes.label: lem:rumor-protocol-conditions

nodes.statement: The calls are independent uniform coordinates, so the events ``$x$ stays uninformed'' and ``$x$ and $y$ stay uninformed'' have product probabilities. The bounds use $(1-x)^k\le1-kx+(kx)^2/2$ and $e^t\le1+2t$ on $[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Theorems 51, 52, 53: push, pull, push--pull, upper bounds
nodes.statement: From any nonempty set of informed nodes on $K_n$, all nodes are informed within $\lceil\log_2n\rceil+\lceil\ln n\rceil+r$ (push), $\lceil\log_2n\rceil+\lceil\log_2\ln n\rceil+r$ (pull) and $\lceil\log_3n\rceil+\lceil\log_2\ln n\rceil+r$ (push--pull) rounds, except with probability at most $Ae^{-\kappa r}$; the expected times are at most $\log_2n+\ln n+B$, $\log_2n+\log_2\ln n+B$ and $\log_3n+\log_2\ln n+B$.
nodes.label: thm:rumor-protocols

nodes.statement: Instantiate Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-total} (push) and Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-total-double} (pull, push--pull) with Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-protocol-conditions}; the middle range is empty since $f=g=\frac12$.

nodes.name: Lower envelopes and joining at a fixed time
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be an observable of a Markov kernel and $(g_i)$, $(\delta_i)$ sequences with $\delta_i\ge0$. If from every state with $V\ge g_i$ the observable falls below $g_{i+1}$ in one round with probability at most $\delta_i$, then from a state with $V\ge g_0$ it is below $g_t$ after $t$ rounds with probability at most $\sum_{i<t}\delta_i$ (the round-by-round form of Lemmas~42 and~50). For a rumor-spreading process: if one round multiplies the expected number of informed nodes by at most $\mu$, then $\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le t]\le\mu^t|S|/m$; and if every state with fewer than $m'$ informed nodes reaches $m$ within $t$ rounds with probability at most $B$, then $\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le s+t]\le\Pr[T(|S|,m')\le s]+B$.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: lem:rumor-lower-generic

nodes.statement: Induction on $t$ for the envelope; Markov's inequality on $E|S_t|\le\mu^t|S|$; the Markov property at time $s$.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Expectations and growth
nodes.statement: After one round from $S$, $E|S'|\le2|S|$ (push, pull) and $E|S'|\le3|S|$ (push--pull), and $E[n-|S'|]=(n-|S|)(1-\frac1n)^{|S|}$, $(n-|S|)(1-\frac{|S|}n)$ and $(n-|S|)(1-\frac1n)^{|S|}(1-\frac{|S|}n)$. Hence $\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le t]\le2^t|S|/m$ (push, pull) and $3^t|S|/m$ (push--pull).
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: lem:rumor-lower-growth

nodes.statement: Sum the exact probabilities of Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-protocol-conditions} over the uninformed nodes, with $1-(1-\frac1n)^k\le\frac kn$; then Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: One round of the final phase; Lemmas 39 and 49
nodes.statement: Let $u=n-|S|$ and $u'$ the number of uninformed nodes after one round. Push, at any level $4\le v\le u$: $\Pr[u'<v/e-v^{3/4}]\le v^{-1/2}$. Pull: $\Pr[u'<u^2/(2n)]\le4n^2/u^3$. Push--pull: $\Pr[u'<u^2/(2en)]\le4e^2n^2/u^3$.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: lem:rumor-lower-round

nodes.statement: Chebyshev's inequality on the lower tail of $u'$, with $\mathrm{Var}[u']\le u$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-variance} with nonpositive covariances) and $E[u']\ge u/e$ (push, from $(1-\frac1n)^k\ge e^{-1}$ for $k<n$), $E[u']=u^2/n$ (pull), $E[u']\ge u^2/(en)$ (push--pull).
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Final phase of push; Theorem 38 for push
nodes.statement: For every $n$, every $S$ with $u=n-|S|$ uninformed nodes and every $t$: $\Pr[T(|S|,n)\le t]\le1600\,e^{(t-\ln u)/2}$.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: thm:rumor-lower-final-push

nodes.statement: Lower envelope (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}) along the explicit targets $g_i=q_i^3(q_i-20)$, $q_i=(ue^{-i})^{1/4}$, which replace the paper's recursive $u_{j+1}=E_0(u_j)$ (Lemma~40). The step $g(qe^{-1/4})\le g(q)/e-g(q)^{3/4}$ reduces to $c^4-20c+20\le0$ for $c=e^{1/4}$; while $q_i\ge40$, round $i$ fails with probability at most $2/q_i^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-round}) and these failure probabilities sum to at most $4e^{(t-\ln u)/2}$; when $q_t<40$ the bound exceeds $1$.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Final phase of pull and push--pull; Theorem 48 with $\ell=2$
nodes.statement: For $n\ge3$, every $S$ with $2|S|\le n$ and every $t\le\log_2\ln n-5$: $\Pr[T(|S|,n)\le t]\le128\,n^{-1/2}$ (pull) and $128e^2n^{-1/2}$ (push--pull).
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: thm:rumor-lower-final-double

nodes.statement: Lower envelope along the double exponential targets $g_i=2n(1/4)^{2^i}$ (pull) and $2en(1/(4e))^{2^i}$ (push--pull), the paper's $\varepsilon_{j+1}=E(\varepsilon_j)/2$, with Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-round}. The paper's exponent $-1+2\alpha\ell$ is replaced by the weaker $-1/2$, which comes from the cruder variance bound and suffices below.
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Theorems 51, 52, 53: push, pull, push--pull, lower bounds
nodes.statement: There are $A$, $B$, $\kappa>0$ and $N$ such that, for $n\ge N$ and one informed node on $K_n$, all nodes are informed within $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+\lfloor\ln n\rfloor-r$ (push), $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-r$ (pull) and $\lfloor\log_3n\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-r$ (push--pull) rounds with probability at most $Ae^{-\kappa r}$; the expected times are at least $\log_2n+\ln n-B$, $\log_2n+\log_2\ln n-B$ and $\log_3n+\log_2\ln n-B$ (stated for every partial sum $\sum_{t<R}\Pr[T>t]$ with $R$ at least the bound).
nodes.section: 42 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: thm:rumor-protocols-lower

nodes.statement: Join the two phases at a fixed time (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}) with $m'=n/2$. Push: after $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor-\lceil r/2\rceil$ rounds at most $n/2$ nodes are informed except with probability $O(2^{-r/2})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-growth}), and from there Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-lower-final-push} bounds the rest. Pull and push--pull: the same with $\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-5$ rounds for the final phase (Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-lower-final-double}), whose $n^{-1/2}$ becomes $e^{-(\ln2/4)r}$ since a nontrivial time forces $r\le2\log_2n$. The tails have rate $\kappa=\ln2/4$; the expectations follow by summing the tail series.

nodes.name: Rounds of neighbour choices
nodes.statement: In a round $r$, every vertex $x$ of a finite graph $G$ samples $k$ neighbours $r(x,0),\dots,r(x,k-1)$. A uniform round is exactly the paper's sampling: $k$ uniform neighbours with replacement, independently for every vertex; $t$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds are averaged with \texttt{Dynamics.expList}. If $G$ is connected and has at least two vertices, rounds exist.
nodes.label: def:choices

nodes.statement: Every vertex of a connected graph with at least two vertices has a neighbour.

nodes.name: COBRA and BIPS
nodes.statement: COBRA from $C_0=C$: $C_{s+1}=\{r_{s+1}(x,i) : x\in C_s,\ i<k\}$. BIPS with persistent source $v$ from $A_0$: $A_{s+1}=\{v\}\cup\{u : \exists i,\ r_{s+1}(u,i)\in A_s\}$.
nodes.label: def:cobra

nodes.name: Time reversal of i.i.d.\ rounds
nodes.statement: For every functional $F$ of $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds, $\mathbb E[F(r_T,\dots,r_1)]=\mathbb E[F(r_1,\dots,r_T)]$.
nodes.label: lem:reverse

nodes.statement: The uniform average over $\mathrm{Fin}\,T\to\alpha$ is invariant under $\omega\mapsto\omega\circ\mathrm{rev}$ (the time-reversal lemma of the shared \texttt{dynamics} package).

nodes.name: Pathwise duality
nodes.statement: For all rounds $r_1,\dots,r_t$: COBRA from $C$ along $r_1,\dots,r_t$ visits $v$ at some time $s\le t$ (time $0$ included) iff BIPS from $\{v\}$ along $r_t,\dots,r_1$ infects a vertex of $C$.
nodes.label: lem:pathwise

nodes.statement: Induction on $t$, generalizing $C$. Both sides say that a chain $x_0\in C$, $x_j=r_j(x_{j-1},i_j)$, reaches $v$ within $t$ steps: COBRA unfolds the first round, BIPS the last round of the reversed sequence.

nodes.name: Theorem 4 of Cooper--Radzik--Rivera
nodes.statement: For every finite graph, every $k$, every vertex $v$, set $C$ and time $t$: $\hat{\mathbb P}(\mathrm{Hit}_C(v)>t\mid C_0=C)=\mathbb P(C\cap A_t=\emptyset\mid A_0=\{v\})$. In particular (equation (2)), $\hat{\mathbb P}(\mathrm{Hit}_u(v)>t)=\mathbb P(u\notin A_t\mid A_0=\{v\})$. The paper assumes $G$ connected and regular and $k\ge1$; none of this is needed.
nodes.label: thm:duality

nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:pathwise} identifies the two events after reversing the rounds, and Lemma~\ref{lem:reverse} says that reversing the rounds preserves their law. The paper proves the theorem instead by induction on $t$ with one-step conditioning.

nodes.name: Second eigenvalue
nodes.statement: $\lambda=\max(\lambda_2,|\lambda_n|)$ for the sorted eigenvalues of $P$ ($0$ if $n<2$).
nodes.label: def:lambda

nodes.name: Spectral core of Lemma~1
nodes.statement: For every set $A$: $\sum_x (d_A(x)/r)^2\le\lambda^2|A|+(1-\lambda^2)|A|^2/n$.
nodes.label: lem:crr-spectral

nodes.statement: $\sum_x(d_A(x)/r)^2=\|P1_A\|^2$; expand $1_A$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis of $P$: the top eigenvector is constant with coefficient $|A|/\sqrt n$, and every other eigenvalue has square at most $\lambda^2$. If $\lambda\ge1$, use $d_A(x)\le r$ and $\sum_x d_A(x)=r|A|$.

nodes.name: Lemma~1, MGF and Chernoff bound
nodes.statement: One BIPS round from $A$ gives $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+(1-\lambda^2)(1-|A|/n))$, $\E e^{-\varphi|A'|}\le\exp(-(1-e^{-\varphi})\E|A'|)$ for every real $\varphi$, and $\Pr(|A'|\le(1-\delta)\mu)\le e^{-\delta^2\mu/2}$ for $\mu\le\E|A'|$, $0<\delta<1$.
nodes.label: lem:crr-growth

nodes.statement: Vertices are infected independently; $u\ne v$ with probability $1-(1-d_A(u)/r)^k\ge 2d_A(u)/r-(d_A(u)/r)^2$. Sum and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-spectral}. The MGF factors over the vertices and $1-x\le e^{-x}$; the Chernoff bound is Markov's inequality with $\varphi=-\log(1-\delta)$.

nodes.name: Lemmas~2 to~4, for an abstract growth process
nodes.statement: Let a round-driven set process have a persistent source, the MGF bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-growth}, growth $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+c(1-|A|/n))$ with $0<c\le1$, be monotone, and have $V$ absorbing. From $\{v\}$ the size exceeds $m\le n/2$ within $13m/c+24C\log n/c^2$ rounds except with probability $n^{-C}$; from $|A_0|\ge4000\log n/c^2$ it reaches $9n/10$ within $T\ge24\log n/c$ rounds except with probability $T n^{-5}$; from $|A_0|\ge9n/10$ (if $4000\log n/c^2\le 9n/10$) it covers $V$ after $T\ge8\log n/c$ rounds except with probability $n^{-5}$. BIPS satisfies the hypotheses with $c=1-\lambda$.
nodes.label: thm:crr-phases

nodes.statement: Lemma~2: the exponential supermartingale $e^{-\varphi|A_t|}$ on the event of staying small, $\varphi=\log(1+c/2)$. Lemma~3: a round with $|A'|<|A|(1+c/23)$ has probability $\le n^{-5}$; union bound over rounds with moving targets. Lemma~4: staying above $9n/10$ and the recursion $\E B_{t+1}\le\theta\E B_t+tn^{-7}$ for the number $B_t$ of healthy vertices. The paper's Lemmas~3 and~4 need minor corrections ($\log_2$ versus $\ln$ doublings; a missing factor $B_0$).

nodes.name: Theorem~2
nodes.statement: If $1-\lambda\ge128\sqrt{\log n/n}$, BIPS from $\{v\}$ has $A_T\ne V$ with probability at most $3/n^3$ for $T\ge60000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$, and $\sum_{s<H}\Pr(A_s\ne V)\le 130000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$.
nodes.label: thm:crr-bips

nodes.statement: Chain the three phases at their first hitting times with $m=\ceil{4000\log n/(1-\lambda)^2}$ and $C=3$. (The paper's proof takes $m=4000\log n/(1-\lambda^2)$, which needs a minor correction: Lemma~3 needs $|A|\ge4000\log n/(1-\lambda)^2$.) For the expectation, restart from the current set: monotonicity and the persistent source give $\Pr(A_{s+T_0}\ne V)\le\Pr(A_s\ne V)/2$.

nodes.name: Theorem~1
nodes.statement: If $1-\lambda\ge128\sqrt{\log n/n}$, COBRA from $\{u\}$ has $\bigcup_{t=1}^T C_t\ne V$ with probability at most $3/n^2$ for $T\ge60002\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$, and every partial tail sum of the cover time is at most $130000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$.
nodes.label: thm:crr-cobra

nodes.statement: Union bound over the missed vertex $w$. Splitting off the first round, missing $w$ at the times $1,\dots,T$ is not hitting $w$ within $T-1$ rounds from $C_1\ne\emptyset$, which by Theorem~\ref{thm:duality} has probability $\Pr(C_1\cap A_{T-1}=\emptyset)\le\Pr(A_{T-1}\ne V)$. For the expectation, restart COBRA from the nonempty set $C_s$ (equation~(1)).

nodes.name: Branching factor $1+p/q$
nodes.statement: A round gives every vertex two neighbour samples and a uniform coin in $\{0,\dots,q-1\}$; a vertex uses its second sample iff its coin is $<p$. COBRA pushes to the used samples, BIPS contacts them.
nodes.label: def:coin

nodes.name: Theorem~4, Corollary~1 and Theorem~3
nodes.statement: The duality holds for the coin processes; with $\rho=p/q$, $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+\rho(1-\lambda^2)(1-|A|/n))$; and for constants $\lambda_0<1$, $\rho_0>0$ there are $C,N$ such that for $n\ge N$, $\lambda\le\lambda_0$ and $\rho\in[\rho_0,1]$ the COBRA cover time with branching factor $1+\rho$ is at most $C\log n$ with probability $1-C/n^2$ and in expectation.
nodes.label: thm:crr-coin

nodes.statement: Both coin processes are target-set processes, whose duality is proved as Theorem~4. A vertex $u\ne v$ is infected with probability $(1+\rho)P_u-\rho P_u^2$, $P_u=d_A(u)/r$; sum and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-spectral}. Then Theorems~\ref{thm:crr-phases} to~\ref{thm:crr-cobra} apply with $c=\min(1,\rho_0(1-\max(\lambda_0,0)))$, and $128\sqrt{\log n/n}\le c$ for $n$ large.

nodes.name: Median dynamics
nodes.statement: Values lie in a linear order. In a round every node samples two nodes uniformly at random (independently, with replacement) and adopts the median of its own value and the two sampled values. With two values this is 2-Choices: a node keeps its value unless both samples hold the other one.
nodes.label: def:median

nodes.name: Threshold reduction
nodes.statement: The median commutes with monotone maps; hence for every threshold $\theta$ the indicator of $\{x_v\ge\theta\}$ evolves, round by round and for the same samples, as the binary median process.
nodes.label: thm:threshold

nodes.statement: $\mathrm{med}(a,b,c)=\max(\min(a,b),\min(\max(a,b),c))$, and monotone maps commute with $\min$ and $\max$.

nodes.name: Validity, range, consensus
nodes.statement: Every new value is a current value, values stay within any interval containing all current values, consensus configurations are fixed, and consensus is reached almost surely.
nodes.label: thm:basic

nodes.statement: The median is one of its arguments; the round in which every node samples node $0$ twice gives consensus and has positive probability; conclude with the shared absorption theorem.

nodes.name: Binary expectation
nodes.statement: With two values and a fraction $p$ of \texttt{true}, the expected number of \texttt{true} after one round is $n(3p^2-2p^3)$, the same cubic as for 3-Majority.
nodes.label: thm:expect

nodes.statement: A \texttt{true} node stays unless both samples are \texttt{false}, a \texttt{false} node switches iff both samples are \texttt{true}.

nodes.name: 2-Choices, w.h.p.
nodes.statement: If $\log n\ge 128$ and the \texttt{true} nodes outnumber the \texttt{false} ones by at least $128\sqrt{n\log n}$, all nodes hold \texttt{true} after $\lceil 128\log n\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-128/n$.
nodes.label: thm:whp

nodes.statement: Phases as in the plurality package: while it is small, the gap grows by a factor $5/4$ per phase except with probability $O(n^{-2})$ (Bernstein); then the minority shrinks by $7/8$ per phase down to $O(\log n)$; a final round reaches consensus except with probability $O(n^{-1/2})$ (Markov). The phases are combined with the nested-phases lemma of the shared layer. The threshold $\log n\ge128$, i.e.\ $n\ge e^{128}$, comes from these crude constants.

nodes.name: 2-Choices from any start
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$, from every binary configuration (possibly perfectly balanced) all nodes agree after $\lceil C\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability at most $C/n$.
nodes.label: thm:binary-any

nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{18}$ and write $g$ for the number of \texttt{true} nodes minus the number of \texttt{false} nodes. \emph{Escape:} the potential $e^{-|g|/(256\sqrt n)}$ contracts in expectation by $e^{-1/65536}$ per round, up to an additive error $e^{1/131072-\sqrt n/512}$: away from balance by Hoeffding's lemma applied at every node, near balance because the next gap has variance at least $n/10$, so by Paley--Zygmund it leaves $[-\sqrt n/4,\sqrt n/4]$ with probability at least $9/64$. Iterating over $\lceil 2^{17}\log n\rceil$ rounds and applying Markov's inequality, $|g|\ge 128\sqrt{n\log n}$ except with probability $2/n$. \emph{Consensus:} Theorem~\ref{thm:whp}, applied to the configuration or to its flip, finishes within $\lceil 128\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability $128/n$.

nodes.name: Reduction to two values
nodes.statement: If every binary configuration fails to reach consensus within $T$ rounds with probability at most $\varepsilon$, then a configuration with $m$ distinct values fails with probability at most $(m-1)\varepsilon$.
nodes.label: thm:of-binary

nodes.statement: If a run has not reached consensus, two nodes hold values $a<b$, and the threshold configuration $\{x_v\ge b\}$, which follows the same rounds by Theorem~\ref{thm:threshold}, has not reached consensus either. Take a union bound over the $m-1$ thresholds above the minimum value.

nodes.name: Consensus from any configuration
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$, from every configuration with values in a linear order (any number of distinct values) all nodes agree after $\lceil C\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability at most $C/n$. This is Theorem~1 of Doerr et al.\ without the adversary.
nodes.label: thm:any

nodes.statement: Consensus is absorbing, so three blocks of $\lceil C_0\log n\rceil$ rounds turn the binary failure bound $C_0/n$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-any} into $(C_0/n)^3$. The union bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:of-binary} over at most $n-1$ thresholds gives $n(C_0/n)^3\le (3C_0+3)/n$, since $C_0^3\le n$ when $\log n\ge 3C_0+3$.

nodes.name: Fast binary consensus from a large gap
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$, if the \texttt{true} nodes outnumber the \texttt{false} ones by at least $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$, all nodes hold \texttt{true} after $\lceil C(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-C/n$.
nodes.section: 50 Many values: the middle one wins fast
nodes.label: thm:binary-fast

nodes.statement: Take $C=128$ and chain one-round moves, each failing with probability at most $n^{-2}$, through four segments: the gap grows by a factor $5/4$ per round until the minority is below $n/4$ ($O(\log(n/\Delta))$ rounds); six rounds bring the minority below $n/8$; it then shrinks quadratically, $m\mapsto\approx 3m^2/n$ (Bernstein), down to $512\log n$ ($O(\log\log n)$ rounds); eight more rounds give consensus. Consensus is absorbing, so the remaining rounds are harmless, and a union bound over the rounds gives the failure probability.
nodes.section: 50 Many values: the middle one wins fast

nodes.name: Margins around a value
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$: if, for a value $v$, the nodes holding a value $\ge v$ outnumber those holding a value $<v$ by at least $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$, and symmetrically the nodes holding a value $\le v$ outnumber those holding a value $>v$ by at least $\Delta$, then all nodes hold $v$ after $\lceil C(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-2C/n$.
nodes.section: 50 Many values: the middle one wins fast
nodes.label: thm:median-fast

nodes.statement: The indicators of $\{x_u\ge v\}$ and of $\{x_u\le v\}$ both evolve as 2-Choices with the same samples (the second because the median is self-dual), with gaps the two margins. When both reach consensus on \texttt{true}, all nodes hold $v$; conclude with Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-fast} (with the same $C=128$) and a union bound.
nodes.section: 50 Many values: the middle one wins fast

nodes.name: An odd number of equally supported values
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$: if the nodes hold $2k+1$ distinct values, each held by $n/(2k+1)$ nodes, and $C(2k+1)\sqrt{n\log n}\le n$, then the middle value is held by all nodes after $\lceil C(\log(2k+1)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-C/n$. This is the deterministic core of the odd case of Theorem~21 of Doerr et al.
nodes.section: 50 Many values: the middle one wins fast
nodes.label: thm:odd-split

nodes.statement: Both margins around the middle value equal $n/(2k+1)\ge C_0\sqrt{n\log n}$, and $\log(n/\Delta)=\log(2k+1)$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:median-fast} with $C=2C_0$.
nodes.section: 50 Many values: the middle one wins fast

nodes.name: Two-sample voting on a graph
nodes.statement: On a simple graph $G$, in a round every vertex samples two neighbours independently and uniformly at random (with replacement) and adopts the median of its own opinion and the two sampled ones; with two opinions it adopts the sampled opinion when the two samples agree. For a majority opinion $a$, the minority $B$ is the set of vertices holding another opinion. $E(S,T)$ is the number of ordered pairs $(u,v)\in S\times T$ of adjacent vertices, so $E(S,S)=2|E(S)|$.
nodes.label: def:graph-voting

nodes.name: Second eigenvalue
nodes.statement: For a $d$-regular graph, $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$ are the eigenvalues of the transition matrix $P=A/d$ and $\lambda_G=\max\{\lambda_2,|\lambda_n|\}$.
nodes.label: def:lambdaG

nodes.name: Expander mixing lemma, the paper's Lemma~3
nodes.statement: On every $d$-regular $n$-vertex graph and for all vertex sets $S,T$, $|E(S,T)-d|S||T|/n|\le\lambda_G\,d\sqrt{|S||T|}$.
nodes.label: lem:eml

nodes.statement: Expand $1_S\cdot P1_T=\sum_k\mu_k s_kt_k$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis. If $\lambda_G<1$, every eigenvector other than the top one has eigenvalue at most $\lambda_2<1$, hence is orthogonal to the all-ones vector, which is fixed by $P$; so the top term is $|S||T|/n$, and Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the others by $\lambda_G\sqrt{|S||T|}$. If $\lambda_G\ge1$, both $E(S,T)$ and $d|S||T|/n$ lie in $[0,d\sqrt{|S||T|}]$.

nodes.name: Small sets are sparse
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_G\le 3/5-\varepsilon$ and $|S|\le\varepsilon n$, then $E(S,S)\le (3/5)\,d|S|$.
nodes.label: lem:sparse

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:eml} with $T=S$, $E(S,S)\le d|S|^2/n+\lambda_Gd|S|\le(\varepsilon+3/5-\varepsilon)d|S|$.

nodes.name: One round, the paper's Lemma~5 at $\alpha=3/10$
nodes.statement: If every superset $S\supseteq B$ with $|S|\le(1+1/\alpha)|B|$ spans at most $\alpha d|S|$ edges, then after one round $\mathbb E|B'|\le(1-(1-2\alpha)(1-3\alpha))|B|=(24/25)|B|$, and $|B'|\le(49/50)|B|$ with probability at least $1-e^{-|B|/4850}$.
nodes.label: lem:phase2

nodes.statement:
Let $p_v$ be the fraction of neighbours of $v$ in $B$ and $y=\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)$, which equals $\sum_{v
otin B}p_v$ by double counting. Then $\mathbb E|B'|=\sum_{v
otin B}p_v^2+\sum_{v\in B}(1-(1-p_v)^2)$. Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2\ge y^2/|B|$. With $C=\{v
otin B:p_v>3/10\}$, the chord bound $p^2\le(3/10)p+(p-3/10)^+$ and the sparsity of $B\cup C$ (which has at most $(13/3)|B|$ vertices) give $\sum_{v
otin B}p_v^2\le(3/10)y+(y-(2/5)|B|)/2$. Altogether $\mathbb E|B'|\le(24/25)|B|-(y-(2/5)|B|)^2/|B|$. The new minority is a sum of independent indicators; the multiplicative Chernoff bound with mean bound $(24/25)m$ and $\delta=1/48$ gives $\Pr(|B'|\ge(49/50)m)\le e^{-m/4850}$ for every $m\ge|B|$.

nodes.name: Theorem~4
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a $d$-regular $n$-vertex graph with $d>0$ and $\lambda_G\le3/5-\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon>0$, and let the minority have size at most $(\varepsilon/5)n$. After $T$ rounds every vertex holds the majority opinion except with probability at most $(24/25)^T|B|+Te^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$. For $T=\lceil C\log n\rceil$ with $C=25000$ the failure probability is at most $1/n+(C\log n+1)e^{-\varepsilon n/C}$, which tends to $0$ for fixed $\varepsilon$.
nodes.label: thm:expander

nodes.statement: While $|B|\le(\varepsilon/5)n$, every superset of $B$ of size at most $(13/3)|B|\le\varepsilon n$ is sparse (Lemma~\ref{lem:sparse}), so by Lemma~\ref{lem:phase2} the expected minority contracts by $24/25$ in every round and one round leaves this region with probability at most $e^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$ (take $m=(\varepsilon/5)n$). By induction on $T$, a $[0,1]$-valued observable bounded by the potential $|B|$ in the region has expectation at most $(24/25)^T|B_0|+Te^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$; apply it to the indicator of not being in consensus. For the $O(\log n)$ form, $(24/25)^T\le e^{-T/25}\le n^{-2}$ and $|B_0|\le n$.

nodes.name: Imbalance and flows
nodes.statement:
The imbalance is $
u=(A-B)/n$, and $\eta=\alpha n/\sqrt{AB}$ for a parameter $\alpha$. The flows of a round are $\Delta_{BA}$, the number of vertices of $B$ that hold $a$ after the round, and $\Delta_{AB}$, the number of vertices of $A$ that no longer hold $a$; so $B'+\Delta_{BA}=B+\Delta_{AB}$. The length of Phase~I is $T_1(
u,c)=\ceil{\log_{5/4}(1/(2
u))}+\ceil{\log_{4/3}(1/(4c))}$.
nodes.section: 52 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance
nodes.label: def:cer-imbalance

nodes.name: The mixing hypothesis of Lemma~2
nodes.statement: A $d$-regular graph satisfies the mixing hypothesis with parameters $\alpha$ and $c$ if $|E(X,Y)-d|X||Y|/n|\le\alpha d\sqrt{|X||Y|}$ for all disjoint $X,Y$ with $|Y|\ge cn$ and $|X|\ge(2/3)\alpha c^{3/2}n$.
nodes.section: 52 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance
nodes.label: def:cer-mixing-prop

nodes.name: Lemma~3
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_G\le\alpha$, the mixing hypothesis holds with $\alpha$ and every $c$.
nodes.section: 52 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance
nodes.label: lem:cer-mixing-prop

nodes.statement: The expander mixing lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:eml}) with $\lambda_G\le\alpha$.
nodes.section: 52 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance

nodes.name: Expected flows
nodes.statement: $\E\Delta_{BA}\ge(A^2B/n^2)(1-2\eta)$ and $\E\Delta_{AB}\le(AB^2/n^2)(1+15\eta)$.
nodes.section: 52 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance
nodes.label: lem:cer-flows-expect

nodes.statement: Let $p_v$ be the fraction of neighbours of $v$ in $B$. A vertex of $B$ adopts $a$ with probability $(1-p_v)^2$ and a vertex of $A$ leaves $a$ with probability $p_v^2$, so $\E\Delta_{BA}=\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2$ and $\E\Delta_{AB}=\sum_{v\in A}p_v^2$. For the first, Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2\ge(E(B,A)/d)^2/B$, and the mixing hypothesis gives $E(B,A)\ge(dAB/n)(1-\eta)$. For the second, the hypothesis bounds the size of $\{v\in A:p_v\ge(1+2^j\eta)B/n\}$ by $A/4^j$; summing $p_v^2$ as a layer cake over these sets, up to the $m$ with $4^m\le n^2/(\eta B^2)<4^{m+1}$, gives the bound, since $(1+3m)\eta\le5$.

nodes.name: Tails of the flows

nodes.name: Theorem~2 of the paper needs a major correction
nodes.statement:
The paper states Theorem~2 with success probability $1-o(1)$ whenever $
u_0\ge K\lambda_G$, on every $d$-regular graph. Its proof applies Lemma~2 with $\alpha=\lambda_G$, whose failure probability is $e^{-\Theta(\lambda_G^2n)}$; this is not $o(1)$ when $\lambda_G$ is of order $1/\sqrt n$ or smaller. On the complete graph, $\lambda_G=1/(n-1)$, so a constant difference $A-B\in\{K+2,K+3\}$ satisfies the hypothesis for $n\ge K+3$; the first round produces fluctuations of order $\sqrt n$ in $A-B$, and by symmetry the initial majority then wins with probability tending to $1/2$. Theorem~ef{thm:cer-theorem2} is the corrected statement: it keeps the hypothesis $
u_0\ge K\lambda_G$ and bounds the failure probability in terms of $
u_0^2n$, which tends to $0$ once $
u_0^2n$ is large compared with $\log\log n$ (\href{https://github.com/formal-dynamics/leanamics/blob/main/median/FORMALIZATION_DIFFERENCES.md#theorem-2-of-the-paper-needs-a-major-correction}{details}).

nodes.name: Adaptive adversary
nodes.statement: An adversary maps the list of rounds played so far (the current one last) and the output of the median rule in the current round to a new configuration; it is $F$-bounded if it recolours at most $F$ nodes, and it uses values of $S$ if every value it writes lies in $S$. The run against the adversary applies, in every round, the median rule and then the adversary. More generally, a perturbed run is any function of the rounds played so far that starts at $x$ and, after every round, differs from the output of the median rule in at most $F$ nodes. A configuration is in almost consensus on $b$ with $K$ exceptions if at most $K$ nodes hold a value other than $b$; almost stable consensus during the times $T_0,\dots,T_0+H$ means almost consensus on the same value $b$ at all these times.
nodes.section: 53 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.label: def:adversary

nodes.name: 2-Choices against an adaptive adversary
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$ and $CF\le\sqrt n$, for every binary configuration, every perturbed run with budget $F$ (in particular, the run against every $F$-bounded adversary) and every $H\ge0$, almost stable consensus with $C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$, except with probability at most $(C\log n+H)/n^2$. This is the two-value case (Theorem~10 of the 2009 version) of the main theorem of Doerr et al.
nodes.section: 53 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.label: thm:binary-adv

nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{20}$, so $F\le\sqrt n/1024$, and let $g$ be the gap and $K=\max(16F,1024\log n)$. Recolouring $F$ nodes moves $g$ by at most $2F$ and the minority by at most $F$. \emph{Escape:} the potential $e^{-|g|/(256\sqrt n)}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-any} grows by at most $e^{1/131072}$ under the recolourings, so it still contracts by $e^{-1/131072}$ per round up to an additive $e^{1/65536-\sqrt n/512}$; after $\lceil 2^{19}\log n\rceil$ rounds Markov's inequality gives $|g|\ge 128\sqrt{n\log n}$ except with probability $2/n^2$. \emph{Growth and saturation} (for $g>0$; otherwise flip): a chain of one-round moves, each failing with probability at most $n^{-2}$ for every recolouring, along sets indexed by time: the gap grows from $G$ to $\min(9G/8,17n/32)$ (Hoeffding: $5G/4$ before the recolouring), then the minority shrinks from $t$ to $\max(15t/16,K)$ (Bernstein: $\max(7t/8,512\log n)$ before the recolouring) and stays below $K$. A union bound over the rounds of the chain and of the window gives the bound.
nodes.section: 53 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary

nodes.name: Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$ and $CF\le\sqrt n$: let $S$ be a set of $m$ legal values containing the values of a configuration $x$. Against every $F$-bounded adversary that only writes values of $S$, and for every $H\ge0$, almost stable consensus with $C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$, except with probability at most $(m-1)(C\log n+H)/n^2$.
nodes.section: 53 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.label: thm:median-adv

nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{20}$. All values of the run lie in $S$. For every legal value $b$, the threshold $u\mapsto[b\le x_u]$ of the run is a perturbed run of 2-Choices with the same budget, because the median commutes with monotone maps and thresholding does not increase the Hamming distance. If, for every legal $b$ above the minimum $m_0$, the threshold run stays in almost consensus on some $c_b$ with $K$ exceptions, let $w$ be the largest legal value with $w=m_0$ or $c_w=\texttt{true}$: the nodes below $w$ are exceptions of the threshold at $w$, and the nodes above $w$ are exceptions of the threshold at the next legal value, so the run is in almost consensus on $w$ with $2K$ exceptions. Conclude with the internal bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-adv} and a union bound over the $m-1$ thresholds.
nodes.section: 53 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary

nodes.name: $k$-party 2-Choices
nodes.statement: Colours lie in any type with decidable equality. In a round every node samples two nodes uniformly at random (independently, with replacement) and adopts their colour if the two samples hold the same colour; otherwise it keeps its own. $c_i$ is the number of nodes of colour $i$, and the number of nodes whose two samples both hold $i$ is denoted $\mathrm{twice}_i$.
nodes.label: def:two-choices

nodes.name: Basic facts and two colours
nodes.statement: Consensus configurations are fixed; $c_i'\le c_i+\mathrm{twice}_i$, so an extinct colour stays extinct. On two colours the rule is the median of the own colour and the two samples. For the same rounds, every node that holds \texttt{true} in the binary median process started from the indicator of colour $i$ holds colour $i$.
nodes.label: lem:tc-basic

nodes.statement: A node that does not hold $i$ adopts $i$ only if both samples hold $i$. With two colours, the new colour is the majority among the own colour and the two samples, that is, their median. For the domination, the indicator of $\{\text{new colour}=i\}$ is at least the median of the three indicators, and the median is monotone; induct on the rounds.

nodes.name: One-round expectations
nodes.statement: $\E c_i'=c_i(1+c_i/n-S/n^2)$; hence $c_r\le c_s$ implies $\E c_r'\le\E c_s'$ (Observation~2.1), and $\E(c_i'-c_j')=(c_i-c_j)(1+(c_i+c_j)/n-S/n^2)$. If every colour other than $i$ has at most $b$ nodes, then $S\le c_i^2+(n-c_i)b$. If $a$ and $b$ are the sizes of the largest and the second largest colour, then $\E(a'-b')\ge(a-b)(1+(a/n)(1-a/n))$.
nodes.label: lem:tc-expect

nodes.statement: A node ends in colour $i$ with probability $(c_i/n)^2+[x_v=i](1-S/n^2)$; sum over the nodes. The map $c\mapsto c(1+c/n-S/n^2)$ is increasing on $c\ge0$ since $S\le n^2$. The aggregation bound is $\sum_{j\ne i}c_j^2\le b\sum_{j\ne i}c_j=b(n-c_i)$, and with $S\le a^2+nb$ the gap formula gives the last bound.

nodes.name: One-round concentration
nodes.statement: Let colour $i$ be a largest colour, with $a=c_i>0$ nodes, and $j\ne i$. For every $\lambda\ge0$, $\Pr(a'-c_j'\le\E(a'-c_j')-\lambda)\le\exp(-\lambda^2/(20a^2/n+4\lambda/3))$ and $\Pr(a'\le\E a'-\lambda)\le\exp(-\lambda^2/(4a^2/n+2\lambda/3))$. In particular, if $128\sqrt{n\log n}\le g\le a$, both probabilities are at most $n^{-12}$ for $\lambda=ga/(8n)$ and $\lambda=ag/(4n)$ respectively.
nodes.label: lem:tc-conc

nodes.statement: Both quantities are sums of independent per-node contributions bounded by $1$ in absolute value. A node of colour $i$ or $j$ contributes only when it leaves its colour, which has probability at most $S/n^2\le a/n$, and any other node joins $i$ or $j$ with probability at most $2a^2/n^2$. Bounding each variance by the second moment about the node's current contribution gives $\mathrm{Var}(a'-c_j')\le10a^2/n$ and $\mathrm{Var}(a')\le2a^2/n$; apply Bernstein's inequality. The exponents are then at least $(g^2/(1344n))\ge12\log n$.

nodes.name: The distance increases, Lemma~2.2
nodes.statement: There are constants $z,C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$: if colour $i$ is the largest, with $a=c_i\le n/2$ nodes, $j$ is the second largest, with $b=c_j$ nodes, and $a-b\ge z\sqrt{n\log n}$, then $a'-b'>(a-b)(1+a/(4n))$ with probability at least $1-C/n^2$.
nodes.label: lem:tc-distance

nodes.statement: Take $z=128$ and $C=2$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:tc-expect} and $a\le n/2$, $\E(a'-b')\ge(a-b)(1+a/(2n))$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:tc-conc} with $\lambda=(a-b)a/(8n)$, the gap falls below $\E(a'-b')-\lambda$ with probability at most $n^{-12}$. No bound on the number of colours is needed.

nodes.name: The coupling, Lemma~2.3, as a stochastic domination
nodes.statement: If $c_c\le c_b$, then $\Pr(c_c'\ge t)\le\Pr(c_b'\ge t)$ for every $t$.
nodes.label: lem:tc-stochdom

nodes.statement: Choose a permutation $\tau$ of the nodes sending every node of colour $c$ to a node of colour $b$. For every node $v$, the sample pairs that make $v$ end in colour $c$ are at most as many as those that make $\tau(v)$ end in colour $b$: a node of another colour adopts a colour of size $m$ on the $m^2$ pairs with both samples on it, a node of that colour keeps it on the $n^2-S+m^2$ pairs that do not agree on another colour, and both counts increase with $m$. Choose a permutation of the sample pairs embedding the first set into the second. The induced bijection of rounds preserves the uniform distribution and maps the rounds with $c_c'\ge t$ into the rounds with $c_b'\ge t$. The paper's coupling, read literally, needs a minor correction (\href{https://github.com/formal-dynamics/leanamics/blob/main/median/FORMALIZATION_DIFFERENCES.md#remarks-on-the-sources}{details}).

nodes.name: One round of the growth phase
nodes.statement: There are constants $z,C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$: if colour $i$ has $a=c_i\le3n/4$ nodes and leads every other colour by at least $g\ge z\sqrt{n\log n}$, then with probability at least $1-C/n^2$ after one round $a'\ge a$ and colour $i$ leads every other colour by at least $g(1+a/(8n))$.
nodes.label: lem:tc-growth-round

nodes.statement: Take $z=128$ and $C=2$, and let $b$ be the second largest colour. For every other colour $j$, Observation~2.1 gives $\E c_j'\le\E b'$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:tc-expect} $\E(a'-c_j')\ge(a-b)(1+(a/n)(1-a/n))\ge g(1+a/(4n))$ since $a\le3n/4$. Lemma~\ref{lem:tc-conc} with $\lambda=ga/(8n)$ bounds the failure for $j$ by $n^{-12}$. The aggregation bound gives $\E a'-a\ge ag/(4n)$, so $a'<a$ has probability at most $n^{-12}$. A union bound over the at most $n$ colours present gives the failure probability $2/n^2$. This replaces the coupling of Lemma~2.3, and the range $a\le3n/4$ (instead of $n/2$) closes the gap before the two-colour phase.

nodes.name: The growth phase
