Off the diagonal the tokens make independent $H$-steps; on the diagonal they move together. The lazy kernel of a graph samples the vertex itself with probability $1/2$ and otherwise a uniformly random neighbour. Rounds can also be composed on the left, $W\mapsto r\circ W$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: def:pairwalk

nodes.name: Duality for every kernel
nodes.statement: For every sampling kernel, the probability that no consensus is reached after $T$ rounds is at most the sum over $v\neq u_0$ of the probability that the tokens started at $v$ and $u_0$ are apart after $T$ steps.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: lem:duality-general

nodes.statement: The voter dynamics on maps started from the identity composes the rounds on the right; composing them on the left gives the same finite-time expectations, since the rounds are independent and identically distributed (induction on $T$, exchanging two finite expectations). The left composition read at two vertices is the two-token walk. Conclude with the pointwise union bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:consensus-time}.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus

nodes.name: Hassin--Peleg Theorem 2.4, tail form
nodes.statement: If from every pair of vertices the tokens are apart after $T_0$ steps with probability at most $1/2$, then consensus fails after $kT_0$ rounds with probability at most $(n-1)2^{-k}$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: thm:hp24

nodes.statement: The diagonal is absorbing, so the probabilities of being apart are submultiplicative in blocks of $T_0$ steps; apply Lemma~\ref{lem:duality-general}.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus

nodes.name: Hitting times of the lazy walk; Fact 2.3
nodes.statement: On a connected graph with Laplacian $L$ and $\mathrm{vol}=\sum_z d_z$, the system $h(y)=0$, $(Lh)(x)=2d_x$ for $x\neq y$ has a nonnegative solution $h_y$, the expected hitting time of $y$ for the lazy walk. It satisfies $\sum_z d_z h_y(z)-\mathrm{vol}\,h_y(x)=\sum_z d_z h_x(z)-\mathrm{vol}\,h_x(y)$ and $h_y(x)+h_x(y)\le 4\,\mathrm{vol}\,(n-1)\le 4n^3$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: lem:hitting

nodes.statement: The maximum principle makes the linear system injective, hence surjective. The identity is the symmetry of $L$. For the bound, $\psi=h_y-h_x$ has energy $\psi^\top L\psi=2\,\mathrm{vol}\,(h_y(x)+h_x(y))$; apply Cauchy--Schwarz along a path from $x$ to $y$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus

nodes.name: Sequential and synchronous walks
nodes.statement: Let the two tokens move one at a time, meeting being checked after each move. If a nonnegative potential $F$ drops by one in expectation under a step of either token, the sequential walks are apart after $T$ steps with probability at most $F/T$. For a lazy kernel, the synchronous tokens are apart after $T+1$ steps with probability at most the average of the indicator of starting apart and the sequential survival; hence at most $3/4$ once $T\ge 2\sup F$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: lem:sequential

nodes.statement: Two inductions on $T$. When the first token lands on the old position of the second, the second stays put with probability at least $1/2$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus

nodes.name: Meeting time of lazy walks; Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: On a connected graph with $n$ vertices, two lazy walks are apart after $3(16n^3+1)\le 51n^3$ steps with probability at most $1/2$, and after $51kn^3$ steps with probability at most $2^{-k}$, from every pair of start vertices.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: thm:meeting-lazy

nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:sequential} to the potential $h_y(x)-\sum_z d_z h_y(z)/\mathrm{vol}+4n^3$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting}, bounded by $8n^3$, then submultiplicativity.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus

nodes.name: Hassin--Peleg Theorem 2.5; Survey Theorem 8
nodes.statement: On every connected graph with $n$ vertices and from every initial colouring, the lazy voter dynamics reaches consensus within $255\,n^3\log n$ rounds with probability at least $1-1/n$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus
nodes.label: thm:hp25

nodes.statement: With $k=\lfloor T/(51n^3)\rfloor$, Lemma~\ref{lem:duality-general} and Theorem~\ref{thm:meeting-lazy} bound the failure probability by $(n-1)2^{-k}\le 1/n$.
nodes.section: 89 Section 2.4 on connected graphs: meeting time and $O(n^3\log n)$ consensus

nodes.name: Bipartite double cover
nodes.statement: The graph $\tilde G=G\times K_2$ has vertices $(a,i)$, $a\in V$, $i\in\{0,1\}$, and $(a,i)\sim(b,j)$ iff $a\sim b$ in $G$ and $i\neq j$. Swapping the layers is an automorphism, degrees are those of $G$, and $\mathrm{vol}\,\tilde G=2\,\mathrm{vol}\,G$.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: def:double-cover

nodes.name: Connectivity of the double cover
nodes.statement: If $G$ is connected and not $2$-colourable, then $\tilde G$ is connected.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: lem:double-cover-connected

nodes.statement: Walks of $G$ lift to $\tilde G$, flipping the layer at every step. If $\tilde G$ were disconnected, ``$(w,0)$ is reachable from $(x_0,0)$'' would be a proper $2$-colouring of $G$.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover

nodes.name: Hitting times on the double cover
nodes.statement: The hitting-time system has a unique solution, so the hitting times of $\tilde G$ satisfy $\tilde h_{(y,1-j)}(x,1-i)=\tilde h_{(y,j)}(x,i)$. A plain step away from $y$ lowers $h_y$ by $2$ in expectation, and a plain step of $\tilde G$ from $(x,i)$ is a plain step of $G$ from $x$ followed by a flip of the layer.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: lem:hitting-flip

nodes.statement: Swapping the layers maps solutions to solutions; the maximum principle gives uniqueness. The first-step equation is the row $x$ of the Laplacian system.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover

nodes.name: Additive drift for two tokens
nodes.statement: If a nonnegative potential $F$ drops by at least $c$ in expectation under one step of the two-token walk from every pair of distinct vertices, then $cT\cdot\Pr[\text{apart after }T\text{ steps}]\le F$.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: lem:additive-drift

nodes.statement: Truncate $F$ to $0$ on the diagonal, show $\mathbb E[F'_T]+c\sum_{t<T}\Pr[\text{apart at }t]\le F'$ by induction on $T$, and use that being apart is antitone in $t$.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover

nodes.name: Exact drift of the potential
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be the Coppersmith--Tetali--Winkler potential of $\tilde G$ (as in Theorem~\ref{thm:meeting-lazy}) and $\Psi(x,y)=\Phi((x,0),(y,0))$. Every hitting time of $\tilde G$ is at most $16n^3$, $0\le\Psi\le 32n^3$, and for $x\neq y$ one synchronous plain step of the two tokens lowers $\Psi$ by exactly $4$ in expectation.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: lem:plain-drift

nodes.statement: The bound is the commute bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting} on $\tilde G$ ($2n$ vertices, volume at most $2n^2$). A synchronous step at $(x,y)$ is, on $\tilde G$, a move of the first token from $(x,0)$ to layer $1$ followed by a move of the second token from $(y,0)$ to layer $1$. Between the two moves the tokens lie in different layers, hence are distinct, and each move lowers $\Phi$ by $2$. The layer symmetry of Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting-flip} returns both tokens to layer $0$.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover

nodes.name: Meeting time of plain walks; Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: On a connected nonbipartite graph with $n$ vertices, two synchronous plain walks are apart after $T$ steps with probability at most $8n^3/T$; hence after $16n^3$ steps with probability at most $1/2$, and after $16kn^3$ steps with probability at most $2^{-k}$, from every pair of start vertices.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: thm:meeting-plain

nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:additive-drift} with $c=4$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:plain-drift} give $4T\cdot\Pr[\text{apart}]\le 32n^3$; then submultiplicativity in blocks.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover

nodes.name: Hassin--Peleg Theorem 2.5, plain walk; Survey Theorem 8 with the nonbipartiteness hypothesis
nodes.statement: On every connected nonbipartite graph with $n$ vertices and from every initial colouring, the plain voter dynamics fails to reach consensus after $16kn^3$ rounds with probability at most $(n-1)2^{-k}$, and reaches consensus within $80\,n^3\log n$ rounds with probability at least $1-1/n$.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover
nodes.label: thm:hp25-plain

nodes.statement: As for Theorem~\ref{thm:hp25}, with $k=\lfloor T/(16n^3)\rfloor$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:meeting-plain}.
nodes.section: 90 Section 2.4 for the plain walk: the bipartite double cover

nodes.name: Volume, conductance, minority side, potential
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{vol}(S)=\sum_{u\in S}d_u$; the conductance $\varphi(G)$ is the minimum of $|\mathrm{cut}(U,V\setminus U)|/\mathrm{vol}(U)$ over $0<\mathrm{vol}(U)\le m$; $\lambda_u$ is the number of neighbours of $u$ with another opinion; for two opinions $s_t$ is the side of smaller volume and $\Psi=\sqrt{\mathrm{vol}(s_t)}$.
nodes.label: def:conductance

nodes.name: Independent coordinates
nodes.statement: Resampling one coordinate of an independent point does not change its law. Consequently centred coordinate functions have additive second and third moments, and if replacing each coordinate function improves $\mathbb{E}f(z+\cdot)$ for all admissible $z$, then the replacement of all of them improves $\mathbb{E}f(c+\sum_i g_i(x_i))$ (BGKM16 Lemma~A.1).
nodes.label: lem:indep

nodes.statement: Reindex the pairs $(x,a)$ by $(x[i\mapsto a],x_i)$; induct over the set of replaced coordinates.

nodes.name: BGKM16 Lemma~2.1, corrected
nodes.statement: If $s_t\neq\emptyset$, then $\mathbb{E}[\Psi_{t+1}\mid s_t]\le\Psi-\sum_{u\in s_t}\lambda_u d_u/(32\Psi^3) \le\Psi-d_{\min}\varphi/(32\Psi)$. The paper prints the sum over all of $V$; this needs a minor correction (the inequality does not hold on the star $K_{1,15}$), and its proof gives the sum over $s_t$ (\href{https://github.com/formal-dynamics/leanamics/blob/main/voter/FORMALIZATION_DIFFERENCES.md#51-lemma-21-of-bgkm16-needs-a-minor-correction}{details}).
nodes.label: lem:bgkm-21

nodes.statement: $\Psi_{t+1}$ is at most the root of the new volume $P+\sum_u X_u$ of the opinion of $s_t$. Replace $X_u$ for $u\notin s_t$ by $Y_u=\lambda_u\mathbf{1}[\text{move}]$ (concavity of $\sqrt{\cdot}$), expand $\sqrt{P+x}$ to third order, and use $\mathbb{E}\Delta'=0$, $\mathbb{E}\Delta'^2\ge\sum_{s_t}\lambda_ud_u/4$, $\mathbb{E}\Delta'^3\le0$. The conductance gives $\sum_{s_t}\lambda_ud_u\ge d_{\min}\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}(s_t)$.

nodes.name: BGKM16 Lemma~2.2 and Theorem~1.1~(i), two opinions
nodes.statement: If $128\,\mathrm{vol}(s_0)\le d_{\min}\varphi T$, the opinions still disagree at time $T$ with probability at most $1/2$; in particular after $128m/(d_{\min}\varphi)$ rounds, and the expected consensus time is at most twice that. On dynamic graphs with fixed degrees the same holds once $128\,\mathrm{vol}(s_0)\le d_{\min}\sum_{t<T}\varphi_t$.
nodes.label: thm:bgkm-two

nodes.statement: The drift lemma of the shared library (FND-5) with drift $d_{\min}\varphi_t/32$; restarting bounds the expected time.

nodes.name: BGKM16 Theorem~1.1~(i), any number of opinions
nodes.statement: There is a constant $b$ such that the expected consensus time is at most $b\,m/(d_{\min}\varphi)$ and consensus holds within $b\,m/(d_{\min}\varphi)$ rounds with probability at least $1/2$, for every number of opinions.
nodes.label: thm:bgkm-many

nodes.statement: Project each opinion to the two-opinion process ``$i$ against the rest''. From $\ell\le\theta$ opinions, after $384\,\mathrm{vol}(V)/(\theta d_{\min}\varphi)$ rounds at most $5\theta/6$ remain with probability at least $1/3$ (BGKM16 Lemma~2.3). Summing over the levels $\theta_j=n(5/6)^j$ gives a geometric series; Markov's inequality gives the probability form.

nodes.name: Multiplicative drift of the potential
nodes.statement: On a graph with $n$ vertices and conductance $\varphi$, from every two-opinion configuration, $\mathbb{E}[\Psi_{t+1}\mid s_t]\le(1-\varphi^2/(32n))\,\Psi(s_t)$. Moreover $1\le\Psi\le n$ before consensus.
nodes.label: lem:bgkm-mul

nodes.statement: $\lambda_ud_u\ge\lambda_u^2$ and Cauchy--Schwarz over the at most $n$ vertices of $s_t$ give $\sum_{s_t}\lambda_ud_u\ge(\sum_{s_t}\lambda_u)^2/n\ge\varphi^2\Psi^4/n$; insert this into Lemma~\ref{lem:bgkm-21}. Volumes are integers and $\mathrm{vol}(s_t)\le m\le n^2$.

nodes.name: BGKM16 Lemma~2.4 and Theorem~1.1~(ii)
nodes.statement: If $96\,n\ln n\le\sum_{t<T}\varphi_t^2$ (static graph: $96\,n\ln n\le\varphi^2T$), the opinions still disagree at time $T$ with probability at most $1/n^2$ for two opinions and at most $1/n$ for any number of opinions, on static graphs and on dynamic graphs with fixed degrees. On a static graph the expected consensus time is at most $2T$.
nodes.label: thm:bgkm-sq

nodes.statement: The multiplicative drift lemma of the shared library (FND-5) gives $\Pr(\Psi_T>0)\le\Psi(s_0)\prod_{t<T}(1-\varphi_t^2/(32n))\le n\cdot e^{-3\ln n}$. For many opinions apply this to each projection ``$i$ against the rest'' (the projection commutes with a round, whatever graph the adversary chooses) and take a union bound over the at most $n$ opinions present initially; restarting bounds the expected time.

nodes.name: BGKM16 Theorem~1.1
nodes.statement: The consensus time is at most $\min\{\tau,\tau'\}$ with probability at least $1/2$: on a static graph for every number of opinions, with $\tau=b\,m/(d_{\min}\varphi)$ and $\tau'=b\,n\ln n/\varphi^2$ for a constant $b$; on a dynamic graph with fixed degrees for two opinions, with $\tau$ the first time with $d_{\min}\sum_{t<\tau}\varphi_t\ge128\,\mathrm{vol}(s_0)$ and $\tau'$ the first time with $\sum_{t<\tau'}\varphi_t^2\ge96\,n\ln n$.
nodes.label: thm:bgkm-min

nodes.statement: Combine Theorems~\ref{thm:bgkm-two}, \ref{thm:bgkm-many} and \ref{thm:bgkm-sq}, using $1/n\le1/2$ for $n\ge2$; with one vertex there is nothing to agree on.

nodes.name: Triangle and a nonuniform matrix
nodes.statement: One white vertex on a triangle wins with probability $1/3$. The stochastic matrix whose two rows are $(1/3,2/3)$ has stationary weights $(1/3,2/3)$, providing a nonuniform invariant example.
nodes.label: lem:examples

nodes.name: Wright--Fisher sampling
nodes.statement: On three individuals, let every offspring pick a uniform parent, itself included. This kernel has self-loops, so it is supported beyond the edges of the triangle. Theorem~2.1 still applies, and one allele copy fixes with probability $1/3$.
nodes.label: lem:wf

nodes.name: Bipartite two-cycle
nodes.statement: On the two-vertex graph, every vertex must copy the other vertex. The alternating coloring flips each round and returns after two rounds; neither coloring is constant. Thus connectedness alone is insufficient.
nodes.label: lem:cycle
